title.zh: 卷七十六 列傳第六十六 隱逸下
title.raw: 卷七十六 列傳第六十六 隱逸下 Volume 76 Biographies 66: Recluses 2

sentences.zh: 臧榮緒 吳苞 徐伯珍 沈麟士 阮孝緒 鄧郁 陶弘景 諸葛璩 劉慧斐 范元琰 庾詵 張孝秀 庾承先 馬樞

translations.literal: Zang Rongxu, Wu Bao, Xu Bozhen, Shen Linshi, Ruan Xiaoxu, Deng Yu, Tao Hongjing, Zhuge Qu, Liu Huifei, Fan Yuanyan, Yu Shen, Zhang Xiaoxiu, Yu Chengxian, Ma Shu
translations.idiomatic: Zang Rongxu, Wu Bao, Xu Bozhen, Shen Linshi, Ruan Xiaoxu, Deng Yu, Tao Hongjing, Zhuge Qu, Liu Huifei, Fan Yuanyan, Yu Shen, Zhang Xiaoxiu, Yu Chengxian, and Ma Shu

sentences.zh: 臧榮緒

translations.literal: Zang Rongxu
translations.idiomatic: Zang Rongxu

sentences.zh: 臧榮緒，東莞莒人也。

translations.literal: Zang Rongxu was a man of Ju in Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Rongxu was a native of Ju in Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 祖奉先，建陵令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Fengxian was Magistrate of Jianling.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Fengxian had served as magistrate of Jianling.

sentences.zh: 父庸人，國子助教。

translations.literal: His father Yongren was an Instructor at the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yongren had been an instructor at the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 榮緒幼孤，躬自灌園，以供祭祀。

translations.literal: Rongxu was orphaned in childhood; he personally tended the garden to supply sacrificial offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in childhood, Rongxu worked his own garden to provide for ancestral offerings.

sentences.zh: 母喪後，乃著嫡寢論，掃灑堂宇，置筵席，朔望輒拜薦焉，甘珍未嘗先食。

translations.literal: After his mother's death he wrote the Treatise on the Principal Mourning Quarters, swept the hall, set out mats and seats, and on the first and fifteenth of each month would bow and present offerings; he never tasted delicacies before offering them.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death he composed the Treatise on the Principal Mourning Quarters, kept the hall swept and furnished with mats and seats, and on the first and fifteenth of every month bowed and presented offerings there—never tasting delicacies before they had been offered.

sentences.zh: 純篤好學，括東、西晉為一書，紀錄志傳百一十卷。

translations.literal: Sincere and devoted in learning, he compiled the Eastern and Western Jin into one work—annals, records, treatises, and biographies in one hundred ten scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Sincere and devoted in scholarship, he compiled the histories of Eastern and Western Jin into a single work of one hundred ten scrolls of annals, records, treatises, and biographies.

sentences.zh: 隱居京口教授。

translations.literal: He lived in seclusion at Jingkou and taught students.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in seclusion at Jingkou, where he taught.

sentences.zh: 齊高帝為揚州刺史，征榮緒為主簿，不到。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gao of Qi was Regional Inspector of Yangzhou, he summoned Rongxu as chief clerk; he did not come.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Emperor Gao of Qi was regional inspector of Yangzhou, he summoned Rongxu to serve as chief clerk, but Rongxu did not accept.

sentences.zh: 建元中，司徒褚彥回啟高帝稱述其美，以置秘閣。

translations.literal: During the Jianyuan era, Grand Marshal Chu Yanhui reported to Emperor Gao praising his excellence, and the work was placed in the Secret Archive.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianyuan reign, Grand Marshal Chu Yanhui reported to Emperor Gao praising his work, and it was deposited in the imperial Secret Archive.

sentences.zh: 榮緒惇愛五經，謂人曰：「昔呂尚奉丹書，武王致齋降位，李、釋教誡，並有禮敬之儀，因甄明至道。

translations.literal: Rongxu cherished the Five Classics with deep affection. He said to people: "In old times Lü Shang received the cinnabar book; King Wu performed fasting and stepped down from his seat. The teachings of the Way and of Buddhism both have rituals of reverence, through which the highest Way is made clear.
translations.idiomatic: Rongxu cherished the Five Classics with deep devotion. He told others: "Long ago Lü Shang received the cinnabar book; King Wu fasted and stepped down from his throne. The teachings of the Way and of Buddhism alike prescribe rituals of reverence, by which the supreme Way is clarified.

sentences.zh: 」乃著拜五經序論。

translations.literal: " Therefore he wrote the Preface and Discourse on Bowing to the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: " On this basis he wrote the Preface and Discourse on Bowing to the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 常以宣尼庚子日生，其日陳五經拜之。

translations.literal: He regularly observed that Confucius was born on the gengzi day; on that day he would display the Five Classics and bow to them.
translations.idiomatic: He held that Confucius was born on a gengzi day; on that day each year he would display the Five Classics and bow before them.

sentences.zh: 自號披褐先生。

translations.literal: He styled himself Master Brown-Robe.
translations.idiomatic: He took for himself the style Master Brown-Robe.

sentences.zh: 又以飲酒亂德，言常為誡。

translations.literal: He also held that wine deranges virtue and made it a constant admonition in speech.
translations.idiomatic: He also held that wine corrupts virtue and made that a constant theme in his teaching.

sentences.zh: 永明六年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the sixth year of Yongming.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year of Yongming.

sentences.zh: 初，榮緒與關康之俱隱在京口，時號為二隱。

translations.literal: Earlier, Rongxu and Guan Kangzhi had both lived in seclusion at Jingkou; at the time they were called the Two Recluses.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Rongxu and Guan Kangzhi had both lived in seclusion at Jingkou, and people called them the Two Recluses.

sentences.zh: 吳苞字天蓋，一字懷德，濮陽鄄城人也。

translations.literal: Wu Bao, courtesy name Tiangai and also styled Huaide, was a native of Juancheng in Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Bao, styled Tiangai and also known as Huaide, was a native of Juancheng in Puyang.

sentences.zh: 儒學，善三禮及老、莊。

translations.literal: He studied Confucian learning and was skilled in the Three Rites and in Laozi and Zhuangzi.
translations.idiomatic: He was trained in Confucian learning and excelled in the Three Rites as well as Laozi and Zhuangzi.

sentences.zh: 宋泰始中過江，聚徒教學。

translations.literal: In the Taishi era of Song he crossed the Yangtze and gathered disciples to teach.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taishi era of Song he crossed south of the Yangtze and gathered students to teach.

sentences.zh: 冠黃葛巾，竹麈尾，蔬食二十餘年。

translations.literal: He wore a yellow ramie cap and carried a bamboo fly-whisk, eating vegetables for more than twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: He wore a yellow ramie cap and carried a bamboo fly-whisk, living on vegetables for more than twenty years.

sentences.zh: 與劉瓛俱于褚彥回宅講授。

translations.literal: Together with Liu Huan he lectured at the residence of Chu Yanhui.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Liu Huan he lectured at Chu Yanhui's residence.

sentences.zh: 瓛講禮，苞講論語、孝經，諸生朝聽瓛，晚聽苞也。

translations.literal: Huan lectured on Rites; Bao lectured on the Analects and the Classic of Filial Piety. The students listened to Huan in the morning and to Bao in the evening.
translations.idiomatic: Huan taught the Rites; Bao taught the Analects and the Classic of Filial Piety. Students attended Huan's lectures in the morning and Bao's in the evening.

sentences.zh: 僧岩，北海人。

translations.literal: Seng Yan was a man of Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: Seng Yan was from Beihai.

sentences.zh: 寥廓無常，人不能測。

translations.literal: Vast and unbounded, changing without pattern—men could not fathom him.
translations.idiomatic: Boundless and unpredictable, he was beyond anyone's reckoning.

sentences.zh: 與劉善明友。

translations.literal: He was friends with Liu Shanming.
translations.idiomatic: He was a friend of Liu Shanming.

sentences.zh: 善明為青州，欲舉為秀才，大驚，拂衣而去。

translations.literal: When Shanming was regional governor of Qingzhou, he wished to nominate him as a flourishing-talent candidate. Seng Yan was greatly startled, shook out his robes, and left.
translations.idiomatic: When Shanming became governor of Qingzhou, he wished to nominate Seng Yan as a provincial candidate. Seng Yan was greatly alarmed, shook out his robes, and walked away.

sentences.zh: 後忽為沙門，棲遲山谷，常以一壺自隨。

translations.literal: Later he suddenly became a monk, lodging in mountain valleys, always carrying a jar with him.
translations.idiomatic: Later he suddenly took monastic vows and dwelt in mountain valleys, always keeping a jar at his side.

sentences.zh: 一旦謂弟子曰：「吾今夕當死。

translations.literal: One day he said to his disciples: "Tonight I shall die.
translations.idiomatic: One day he told his disciples: "I shall die tonight.

sentences.zh: 壺中大錢一千，以通九泉之路，蠟燭一挺，以照七尺之屍。

translations.literal: In the jar are a thousand large coins to pay the way to the Nine Springs, and one candlestick to light the seven-foot corpse."
translations.idiomatic: In the jar are a thousand large coins to open the road to the Nine Springs, and one candle to light my seven-foot body."

sentences.zh: 」至夜而亡。

translations.literal: When night came he died.
translations.idiomatic: When night fell, he died.

sentences.zh: 時人以為知命。

translations.literal: People of the time took this as knowledge of fate.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time regarded this as foreknowledge of his fate.

sentences.zh: 蔡薈字休明，陳留人。

translations.literal: Cai Hui, courtesy name Xiuming, was a man of Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Hui, styled Xiuming, was from Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 清抗不與俗人交。

translations.literal: Pure and aloof, he did not associate with men of the world.
translations.idiomatic: Pure and aloof, he kept company with no ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 李撝謂江學曰：「古人稱安貧清白曰夷，涅而不緇曰白，至如蔡休明者，可不謂之夷白乎。」

translations.literal: Li Hang said to Jiang Xue: "The ancients called one who rests content in poverty and keeps himself pure 'yi,' and one who is smeared yet does not turn black 'bai.' As for Cai Xiuming, can he not be called yi-bai?"
translations.idiomatic: Li Hang said to Jiang Xue: "The ancients called one who rests content in poverty and keeps himself pure yi, and one who is stained yet does not turn black bai. As for Cai Xiuming, can he not be called yi-bai?"

sentences.zh: 又有魯國孔嗣之字敬伯，宋時與齊高帝俱為中書舍人，並非所好。

translations.literal: There was also Kong Sizhi of Lu, courtesy name Jingbo, who in Song times had served with Emperor Gao of Qi as Secretaries in the Palace Secretariat—neither liked the post.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Kong Sizhi of Lu, styled Jingbo, who in Song times had served with the future Emperor Gao of Qi as secretaries in the Palace Secretariat—neither man cared for the office.

sentences.zh: 自廬江郡守去官，隱居鍾山。

translations.literal: He resigned from his post as Administrator of Lujiang and lived in seclusion on Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned as administrator of Lujiang and lived in seclusion on Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以為太中大夫，卒。

translations.literal: The court appointed him Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed him Grand Master of Splendid Happiness; he died in that post.

sentences.zh: 徐伯珍

translations.literal: Xu Bozhen
translations.idiomatic: Xu Bozhen

sentences.zh: 徐伯珍字文楚，東陽太末人也。

translations.literal: Xu Bozhen, courtesy name Wenchu, was a native of Taimo in Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Bozhen, styled Wenchu, was a native of Taimo in Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 祖、父並郡掾史。

translations.literal: His grandfather and father had both been clerks in the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Both his grandfather and father had served as commandery clerks.

sentences.zh: 伯珍少孤貧，學書無紙，常以竹箭、箬葉、甘蕉及地上學書。

translations.literal: Bozhen was orphaned and poor in youth; he had no paper for learning to write and often practiced on bamboo slips, zong leaves, plantain leaves, and the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor as a youth, Bozhen had no paper for calligraphy and often practiced writing on bamboo slips, zong leaves, plantain leaves, and the bare ground.

sentences.zh: 山水暴出，漂溺宅舍，村鄰皆奔走，伯珍累床而坐，誦書不輟。

translations.literal: A mountain flood burst forth and inundated his dwelling; the villagers all fled, but Bozhen sat on stacked beds and recited his books without pause.
translations.idiomatic: When a mountain torrent burst out and flooded his house, the neighbors all fled, but Bozhen sat atop stacked beds and went on reciting his texts without interruption.

sentences.zh: 叔父璠之與顏延之友善，還祛蒙山立精舍講授，伯珍往從學。

translations.literal: His uncle Fan Zhi was on friendly terms with Yan Yanzhi; he returned to Qumeng Mountain, established a hermitage, and lectured there, and Bozhen went to study under him.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Fan Zhi was a friend of Yan Yanzhi; Fan Zhi returned to Qumeng Mountain, built a hermitage, and taught there, and Bozhen went to study with him.

sentences.zh: 積十年，究尋經史，遊學者多依之。

translations.literal: After ten years he had thoroughly investigated the classics and histories, and many traveling scholars relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: After ten years he had mastered the classics and histories, and many traveling scholars came to rely on him.

sentences.zh: 太守琅邪王曇生、吳郡張淹並加禮辟，伯珍應召便退，如此者凡十二焉。

translations.literal: The administrators Wang Tansheng of Langye and Zhang Yan of Wu Commandery both honored him with summonses; Bozhen would answer the call and then withdraw—twelve times in all.
translations.idiomatic: The administrators Wang Tansheng of Langye and Zhang Yan of Wu both honored him with official summonses; Bozhen would answer each call and then withdraw—twelve times in all.

sentences.zh: 征士沈儼造膝談論，申以素交。

translations.literal: The recluse-scholar Shen Yi came to speak with him knee to knee and renewed their old friendship.
translations.idiomatic: The recluse Shen Yi came to speak with him face to face and renewed their longstanding friendship.

sentences.zh: 吳郡顧歡擿出尚書滯義，伯珍詶答，甚有條理，儒者宗之。

translations.literal: Gu Huan of Wu Commandery raised obscure points in the Documents; Bozhen answered them with great order, and Confucian scholars looked up to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gu Huan of Wu Commandery raised obscure points in the Documents, Bozhen's replies were so well ordered that scholars looked to him as a model.

sentences.zh: 好釋氏、老、莊，兼明道術。

translations.literal: He loved Buddhist teaching, Laozi, and Zhuangzi, and was also versed in the arts of the Way.
translations.idiomatic: He was drawn to Buddhism, Laozi, and Zhuangzi, and was also versed in Daoist arts.

sentences.zh: 歲嘗旱，伯珍筮之，如期而雨。

translations.literal: In years when drought occurred, Bozhen would divine by milfoil; rain came on the day he predicted.
translations.idiomatic: In drought years Bozhen would cast milfoil stalks; rain fell on the day he foretold.

sentences.zh: 舉動有禮，過曲木之下，趍而避之。

translations.literal: In bearing and movement he was observant of ritual; passing beneath a bent tree, he would quicken his step to avoid it.
translations.idiomatic: In bearing and movement he was scrupulously observant of ritual; passing beneath a bent tree, he would quicken his step to avoid it.

sentences.zh: 早喪妻，晚不復重娶，自比曾參。

translations.literal: He lost his wife early and in later years did not marry again, comparing himself to Zeng Shen.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his wife early and never remarried in later years, comparing himself to Zeng Shen.

sentences.zh: 宅南九里有高山，班固謂之九岩山，後漢龍丘萇隱處也。

translations.literal: Nine li south of his dwelling stood a high mountain that Ban Gu called Jiuyan Mountain—the place where Longqiu Chang of Later Han had lived in seclusion.
translations.idiomatic: Nine li south of his home stood a high mountain that Ban Gu called Jiuyan Mountain—the place where Longqiu Chang of Later Han had lived in seclusion.

sentences.zh: 山多龍須檉柏，望之五采，世呼為婦人岩。

translations.literal: The mountain was rich in dragon-whisker cypress and arborvitae; viewed from afar they showed five colors, and the world called it Lady's Rock.
translations.idiomatic: The slopes were thick with dragon-whisker cypress and arborvitae; seen from afar they shimmered in five colors, and people called the place Lady's Rock.

sentences.zh: 二年，伯珍移居之，階戶之間，木生皆連理。

translations.literal: In the second year he moved his dwelling there; between steps and doorways every tree that grew showed interlaced trunks.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the reign he moved there; between his steps and doorways every tree that sprang up grew with interlaced trunks.

sentences.zh: 門前生梓樹，一年便合抱。

translations.literal: Before his gate a catalpa tree grew; within a year its trunk could be embraced.
translations.idiomatic: A catalpa sprang up before his gate and within a year its trunk was thick enough to embrace.

sentences.zh: 館東石壁，夜忽有赤光洞照，俄爾而滅。

translations.literal: On the stone cliff east of his lodge, red light suddenly shone through the night and in a moment vanished.
translations.idiomatic: On the stone cliff east of his lodge, red light suddenly blazed through the night and then vanished.

sentences.zh: 白雀一雙棲其戶牖，論者以為隱德之感焉。

translations.literal: A pair of white magpies nested at his windows and doors; commentators took this as a response to his hidden virtue.
translations.idiomatic: A pair of white magpies nested at his windows and doors; commentators took this as a sign responding to his hidden virtue.

sentences.zh: 刺史豫章王辟議曹從事，不就。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yuzhang, as regional inspector, summoned him as an aide in the Bureau of Deliberation, but he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yuzhang, serving as regional inspector, summoned him as an aide in the Bureau of Deliberation, but he declined.

sentences.zh: 家甚貧窶，兄弟四人皆白首相對，時人呼為「四皓」。

translations.literal: His household was very poor; all four brothers sat facing one another with white hair, and people of the time called them the Four Hoary Ones.
translations.idiomatic: His household was desperately poor; all four brothers sat facing one another with white hair, and people called them the Four Hoary Ones.

sentences.zh: 建武四年卒，年八十四。

translations.literal: He died in the fourth year of Jianwu, aged eighty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Jianwu, at the age of eighty-four.

sentences.zh: 受業生凡千餘人。

translations.literal: His enrolled students numbered more than a thousand in all.
translations.idiomatic: More than a thousand students studied under him in all.

sentences.zh: 伯珍同郡婁幼瑜字季玉，亦聚徒教授，不應徵辟，彌為臨川王映所賞異，著禮捃拾三十卷。

translations.literal: Lou Youyu of the same commandery as Bozhen, courtesy name Jiyu, also gathered disciples to teach and did not answer summonses; he was especially admired by Prince Ying of Linchuan and wrote Gatherings from the Rites in thirty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Youyu of the same commandery, styled Jiyu, likewise gathered students to teach and declined all official summonses; Prince Ying of Linchuan especially admired him. He wrote Gatherings from the Rites in thirty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 沈麟士

translations.literal: Shen Linshi
translations.idiomatic: Shen Linshi

sentences.zh: 沈麟士字雲禎，吳興武康人也。

translations.literal: Shen Linshi, courtesy name Yunzhen, was a native of Wukang in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Linshi, styled Yunzhen, was a native of Wukang in Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 祖膺期，晉太中大夫。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yingqi was a Grand Master of Splendid Happiness under Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yingqi had been a Grand Master of Splendid Happiness under Jin.

sentences.zh: 父虔之，宋樂安令。

translations.literal: His father Qianzhi was Magistrate of Le'an under Song.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qianzhi had served as magistrate of Le'an under Song.

sentences.zh: 麟士幼而俊敏，年七歲，聽叔父岳言玄。

translations.literal: Linshi was clever and quick from childhood; at age seven he listened as his uncle Yue spoke on the arcane.
translations.idiomatic: Linshi was clever and quick from childhood; at the age of seven he listened while his uncle Yue discoursed on arcane learning.

sentences.zh: 賓散，言無所遺失。

translations.literal: When the guests dispersed, not a word had been lost from his memory.
translations.idiomatic: When the guests left, he had forgotten not a word.

sentences.zh: 嶽撫其肩曰：「若斯文不絕，其在爾乎。

translations.literal: Yue patted his shoulder and said: "If this culture is not cut off, will it not be through you?
translations.idiomatic: Yue patted his shoulder and said: "If this tradition is not lost, will it not be through you?

sentences.zh: 」及長，博通經史，有高尚之心。

translations.literal: " When he grew up he mastered the classics and histories and had a lofty mind.
translations.idiomatic: " When he grew to manhood he mastered the classics and histories and cherished a lofty, retiring spirit.

sentences.zh: 親亡，居喪盡禮。

translations.literal: When his parents died he observed mourning to the full in ritual.
translations.idiomatic: When his parents died he observed mourning with full ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 服闋，忌日輒流淚彌旬。

translations.literal: When mourning was completed, on each anniversary of a parent's death he would weep for ten days.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning ended, on each anniversary of a parent's death he wept for ten days on end.

sentences.zh: 居貧織簾誦書，口手不息，鄉里號為織簾先生。

translations.literal: Living in poverty he wove bamboo curtains while reciting books, mouth and hand never resting; the neighborhood called him Master Curtain-Weaver.
translations.idiomatic: Living in poverty he wove bamboo curtains while reciting texts, never pausing with mouth or hand; neighbors called him Master Curtain-Weaver.

sentences.zh: 嘗為人作竹誤傷手，便流淚而還。

translations.literal: Once while making bamboo work for someone he accidentally injured his hand and at once wept and went home.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while making bamboo work for someone, he accidentally cut his hand and at once wept and went home.

sentences.zh: 同作者謂曰：「此不足損，何至涕零。

translations.literal: His fellow workers said to him: "This is no great harm—why shed tears?
translations.idiomatic: His fellow workers said: "This is no great injury—why weep?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「此本不痛，但遺體毀傷，感而悲耳。

translations.literal: " He answered: "It does not hurt in itself, but the body I received from my parents has been harmed—I am moved to grief.
translations.idiomatic: " He answered: "It does not hurt, but the body I received from my parents has been harmed—that is why I grieve.

sentences.zh: 」嘗行路，鄰人認其所著屐，麟士曰：「是卿屐邪？

translations.literal: " Once on the road a neighbor recognized the sandals he was wearing. Linshi said: "Are these your sandals?
translations.idiomatic: " Once on the road a neighbor recognized the sandals he was wearing. Linshi said: "Are these yours?

sentences.zh: 」即跣而反。

translations.literal: " He at once went barefoot and turned back.
translations.idiomatic: " He immediately went barefoot and turned back.

sentences.zh: 鄰人得屐，送前者還之，麟士曰：「非卿屐邪？

translations.literal: The neighbor recovered the sandals and sent the man who had taken them to return them. Linshi said: "Are these not your sandals?
translations.idiomatic: The neighbor recovered the sandals and sent the man who had taken them back with them. Linshi said: "Aren't these yours after all?

sentences.zh: 」笑而受之。

translations.literal: " He smiled and accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: " He smiled and accepted them.

sentences.zh: 宋元嘉末，文帝令僕射何尚之抄撰五經，訪舉學士，縣以麟士應選。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuanjia era of Song, Emperor Wen ordered the Director of the Secretariat He Shangzhi to compile the Five Classics and to seek out and recommend scholars; the district nominated Linshi for selection.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuanjia era, Emperor Wen of Song ordered Director He Shangzhi to compile the Five Classics and to seek out scholars; the district nominated Linshi.

sentences.zh: 不得已至都，尚之深相接。

translations.literal: Unable to refuse, he came to the capital; Shangzhi received him with deep courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to refuse, he went to the capital, where Shangzhi received him with great warmth.

sentences.zh: 及至，尚之謂子偃曰：「山藪故多奇士，沈麟士，黃叔度之流也，豈可澄清淆濁邪。

translations.literal: When he arrived, Shangzhi said to his son Yan: "Mountains and marshes always harbor extraordinary men. Shen Linshi is of the same sort as Huang Shudu—how could one clarify what is already pure or stir what is already muddy?
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, Shangzhi said to his son Yan: "Mountains and marshes always breed extraordinary men. Shen Linshi is of the same stamp as Huang Shudu—how could one try to clarify what is already pure or stir what is already still?

sentences.zh: 汝師之。」

translations.literal: Take him as your teacher."
translations.idiomatic: Take him as your teacher."

sentences.zh: 麟士嘗苦無書，因遊都下，曆觀四部畢，乃歎曰：「古人亦何人哉。

translations.literal: Linshi had once suffered from lack of books; he therefore traveled to the capital, went through all four sections of the library, and sighed: "The men of old—what sort of men were they?
translations.idiomatic: Linshi had long lacked books; he therefore went to the capital, read through all four sections of the imperial library, and sighed: "What manner of men were the ancients?

sentences.zh: 」少時稱疾歸鄉，不與人物通。

translations.literal: " Before long he pleaded illness and returned to his native place, having no dealings with others.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long he pleaded illness and returned home, keeping company with no one.

sentences.zh: 養孤兄子，義著鄉曲。

translations.literal: He raised his orphaned elder brother's son; his righteousness was renowned in the district.
translations.idiomatic: He raised his orphaned elder brother's son, and his righteousness was renowned throughout the district.

sentences.zh: 或勸之仕，答曰：「魚縣獸檻，天下一契。

translations.literal: Some urged him to take office. He answered: "Fish strung on a line, beasts in a pen—the world is one pattern.
translations.idiomatic: When some urged him to take office, he answered: "Fish on the line, beasts in the pen—the world is all one pattern.

sentences.zh: 聖人玄悟，所以每履吉先。

translations.literal: The sage penetrates the arcane and therefore always treads auspicious ground first.
translations.idiomatic: The sage penetrates the arcane and therefore always treads auspicious ground before others.

sentences.zh: 吾誠未能景行坐忘，何為不希企日損。

translations.literal: I truly cannot yet follow the exemplary conduct of sitting in forgetfulness—why should I not aspire to daily diminishment?
translations.idiomatic: I truly cannot yet follow the exemplary path of sitting in forgetfulness—why should I not aspire to diminish myself day by day?

sentences.zh: 」乃作玄散賦以絕世。

translations.literal: " He then wrote the Rhapsody on Withdrawal into the Arcane to break with the world.
translations.idiomatic: " He then wrote the Rhapsody on Withdrawal into the Arcane to renounce the world.

sentences.zh: 太守孔山士辟不應，宗人徐州刺史曇慶、侍中懷文、左率勃來候之，麟士未嘗答也。

translations.literal: The Administrator Kong Shanshi summoned him but he did not respond. His clansmen—the regional inspector of Xuzhou Tanqing, the Palace Attendant Huaiwen, and the Left Commander Bo—came to visit him, but Linshi never answered.
translations.idiomatic: Administrator Kong Shanshi summoned him, but he did not respond. His kinsmen—Tanqing, regional inspector of Xuzhou; Huaiwen, palace attendant; and Bo, left commander—came to visit him, but Linshi never replied.

sentences.zh: 隱居余不吳差山，講經教授，從學士數十百人，各營屋宇，依止其側，時為之語曰：「吳差山中有賢士，開門教授居成市。

translations.literal: He lived in seclusion on Wucha Mountain in Yuyu, lecturing on the classics and teaching; several hundred students followed him, each building a dwelling and settling beside him. People of the time made a saying: "On Wucha Mountain in Yuyu there is a worthy man; he opens his gate to teach and dwellings form a market.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in seclusion on Wucha Mountain in Yuyu, lecturing on the classics; several hundred students followed him, each building a house nearby. A saying of the time ran: "On Wucha Mountain in Yuyu lives a worthy man; he opens his gate to teach and the neighborhood becomes a town.

sentences.zh: 」麟士重陸機連珠，每為諸生講之。

translations.literal: " Linshi prized Lu Ji's Linked Pearls and often lectured on them for his students.
translations.idiomatic: " Linshi prized Lu Ji's Linked Pearls and often lectured on them for his students.

sentences.zh: 征北張永為吳興，請麟士入郡。

translations.literal: Zhang Yong, Commander-in-chief for the North, was governor of Wuxing and invited Linshi into the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yong, Commander-in-chief for the North, was governor of Wuxing and invited Linshi to visit the commandery seat.

sentences.zh: 麟士聞郡後堂有好山水，即戴安道游吳興，因古墓為山池也。

translations.literal: Linshi had heard that behind the commandery hall there was fine landscape; it was where Dai Andao had visited Wuxing and fashioned hills and pools from old tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Linshi had heard that behind the commandery hall lay fine landscape—the place where Dai Andao had visited Wuxing and fashioned hills and pools from old tombs.

sentences.zh: 欲一觀之，乃往停數月。

translations.literal: Wishing to view it once, he went and stayed several months.
translations.idiomatic: Wishing to see it once, he went and stayed several months.

sentences.zh: 永欲請為功曹，麟士曰：「明府德履沖素，留心山谷，是以被褐負杖，忘其疲病。

translations.literal: Yong wished to invite him as Registrar. Linshi said: "Your Excellency's virtue and conduct are pure and simple; your heart rests in mountain valleys. For this reason I wear coarse cloth and lean on my staff, forgetting my weariness and illness.
translations.idiomatic: Yong wished to appoint him registrar. Linshi said: "Your Excellency's virtue is pure and unadorned; your heart rests in mountain valleys. That is why I wear coarse cloth and lean on my staff, forgetting my weariness and illness.

sentences.zh: 必欲飾渾沌以蛾眉，冠越客于文冕，走雖不敏，請附高節，有蹈東海死耳，不忍受此黔劓。

translations.literal: " If you must adorn primordial chaos with moth eyebrows and crown a Yue guest in a ceremonial cap, though I am untalented, I beg to attach myself to lofty integrity; I have only drowning myself in the eastern sea— I cannot bear to suffer this branding and mutilation.
translations.idiomatic: " If you insist on painting primordial simplicity with cosmetics and crowning a rustic from Yue in court robes, though I am no worthy man, I would rather cleave to noble principle— I would sooner throw myself into the eastern sea than endure this disfigurement.

sentences.zh: 」永乃止。

translations.literal: " Yong then desisted.
translations.idiomatic: " Yong then dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 升明末，太守王奐，永明中，中書郎沈約並表薦之，征皆不就。

translations.literal: At the end of the Shengming era, Administrator Wang Huan; during Yongming, Secretariat Gentleman Shen Yue all submitted memorials recommending him. Summonses came, but he never accepted.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Shengming era, Administrator Wang Huan recommended him; during Yongming, Secretariat Gentleman Shen Yue did the same. Imperial summons came, but he never accepted office.

sentences.zh: 乃與約書曰：「名者實之賓，本所不庶。

translations.literal: He then wrote to Yue, saying: "Fame is the guest of reality; it was never what I hoped for.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote to Yue, saying: "Fame is but the shadow of substance— it was never what I sought.

sentences.zh: 中央無心，空勤南北。

translations.literal: The center has no heart; vainly toiling north and south.
translations.idiomatic: The court has no true intent; one toils in vain between north and south.

sentences.zh: 為惠反凶，將在於斯。」

translations.literal: Doing good turns to harm— that will lie in this."
translations.idiomatic: Kindness turned to injury will come of this."

sentences.zh: 麟士無所營求，以篤學為務，恒憑素幾鼓素琴，不為新聲。

translations.literal: Linshi sought nothing for himself and made devoted study his task; he always leaned on a plain couch and played a plain zither, never performing new compositions.
translations.idiomatic: Linshi desired nothing for himself and devoted himself to serious study; he always sat at a plain desk and played an unadorned zither, never performing fashionable new pieces.

sentences.zh: 負薪汲水，並日而食。

translations.literal: He carried firewood and drew water, eating but once every two days.
translations.idiomatic: He carried firewood and drew water, eating only on alternate days.

sentences.zh: 守操終老，讀書不倦。

translations.literal: He kept his principles to the end of his life, never weary of reading.
translations.idiomatic: He held to his principles until old age and never tired of reading.

sentences.zh: 遭火燒書數千卷，年過八十，耳目猶聰明，以反故抄寫，火下細書，復成二三千卷，滿數十篋。

translations.literal: A fire burned several thousand scrolls of his books; past eighty, his eyes and ears were still keen; he recopied from memory of familiar texts, writing fine script by lamplight, producing another two or three thousand scrolls filling dozens of cases.
translations.idiomatic: A fire destroyed several thousand scrolls of his library; yet past eighty his sight and hearing remained sharp. He copied from memory by lamplight in a fine hand and produced another two or three thousand scrolls, filling dozens of cases.

sentences.zh: 時人以為養身靜默所致。

translations.literal: People of the time attributed this to his nourishing the body through quiet stillness.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time believed this came from his life of quiet self-cultivation.

sentences.zh: 制黑蝶賦以寄意。

translations.literal: He composed the Rhapsody on the Dark Butterfly to express his meaning.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Rhapsody on the Dark Butterfly to give voice to his sentiments.

sentences.zh: 著周易兩系、莊子內篇訓。

translations.literal: He authored commentaries on the Two Appendices of the Book of Changes and the Inner Chapters of Zhuangzi.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote commentaries on the Two Appendices of the Book of Changes and the Inner Chapters of Zhuangzi.

sentences.zh: 注易經、禮記、春秋、尚書、論語、孝經、喪服、老子要略數十卷。

translations.literal: He annotated the Classic of Changes, Book of Rites, Spring and Autumn Annals, Documents, Analects, Classic of Filial Piety, Record of Mourning Garb, and Essential Outline of Laozi— dozens of scrolls in all.
translations.idiomatic: He annotated the Classic of Changes, Book of Rites, Spring and Autumn Annals, Documents, Analects, Classic of Filial Piety, Record of Mourning Garb, and Essential Outline of Laozi— several dozen scrolls in all.

sentences.zh: 梁天監元年，與何點同征，又不就。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjian under Liang, he was summoned together with He Dian, and again did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Liang's Tianjian reign, he was summoned together with He Dian, and again refused to serve.

sentences.zh: 二年，卒於家，年八十五。

translations.literal: In the second year he died at home, aged eighty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he died at home, at the age of eighty-five.

sentences.zh: 以楊王孫、皇甫謐深達生死而終禮矯俗，乃自為終制，遺令：「氣絕剔被，取三幅布以覆屍。

translations.literal: Because Yang Wangsun and Huangfu Mi deeply understood life and death yet ended by observing rites that corrected custom, he himself drew up final arrangements, leaving instructions: "When breath ceases, remove the quilt and take three bolts of cloth to cover the corpse.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yang Wangsun and Huangfu Mi had deeply grasped life and death yet still ended by using funeral rites to reform vulgar custom, he drew up his own final arrangements and left instructions: "When breath fails, strip off the quilt and take three bolts of cloth to cover the body.

sentences.zh: 及斂，仍移布於屍下，以為斂服。

translations.literal: When dressing the body for burial, still move the cloth beneath the corpse to serve as burial garments.
translations.idiomatic: When the body is prepared for burial, move the cloth beneath the corpse to serve as its shroud.

sentences.zh: 反被左右兩際以周上，不復製覆被。

translations.literal: Fold the quilt back over the left and right edges to wrap the top; do not make another covering quilt.
translations.idiomatic: Fold the quilt back over the left and right edges to wrap the top; do not prepare another covering quilt.

sentences.zh: 不須沐浴唅珠。

translations.literal: No bathing or placing pearls in the mouth is needed.
translations.idiomatic: Do not bathe the body or place pearls in the mouth.

sentences.zh: 以本裙衫、先著褌，凡二服，上加單衣幅巾履枕，棺中唯此。

translations.literal: Use one's own skirt-robe and garments already worn beneath, two sets in all; over these add a single garment, kerchief, shoes, and pillow— only these in the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: Use the skirt-robe and undergarments already being worn— two sets in all— and over them add a single outer garment, kerchief, shoes, and pillow. Nothing else goes into the coffin.

sentences.zh: 依士安用孝經。

translations.literal: Follow Shi'an's use of the Classic of Filial Piety.
translations.idiomatic: Follow Huangfu Mi's practice of reciting the Classic of Filial Piety at the funeral.

sentences.zh: 既殯不復立靈座，四節及祥，權鋪席於地，以設玄酒之奠。

translations.literal: Once encoffined, do not again set up a spirit seat; at the four seasonal observances and the end of mourning, temporarily spread mats on the ground and set out offerings of dark wine.
translations.idiomatic: Once the body is encoffined, do not set up a spirit seat again; at the four seasonal observances and the end of mourning, simply spread mats on the ground and offer dark wine.

sentences.zh: 人家相承漆棺，今不復爾。

translations.literal: Families have handed down lacquered coffins— do this no longer.
translations.idiomatic: Families have long used lacquered coffins— do not do so now.

sentences.zh: 亦不須旐。

translations.literal: Banners are also not needed.
translations.idiomatic: Funeral banners are not needed either.

sentences.zh: 成服後即葬，作塚令小，後祔更作小塚於濱。

translations.literal: Bury immediately after donning mourning garments; make the mound small; later, when adding a secondary burial, make another small mound by the riverbank.
translations.idiomatic: Bury immediately after the mourning garments are donned; keep the mound small; when a later joint burial is added, make another small mound by the riverbank.

sentences.zh: 合葬非古也。

translations.literal: Joint burial is not ancient custom.
translations.idiomatic: Joint burial is not the ancient way.

sentences.zh: 塚不須聚土成墳，使上與地平。

translations.literal: The mound need not heap earth into a tomb; let it level with the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Do not heap earth into a high tomb; let the surface lie level with the ground.

sentences.zh: 王祥終制亦爾。

translations.literal: Wang Xiang's final arrangements were the same.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiang's funeral instructions were the same.

sentences.zh: 葬不須軟車、靈舫、魌頭也。

translations.literal: At burial there is no need for cushioned carriage, spirit barge, or demon-mask escorts.
translations.idiomatic: At burial there is no need for cushioned hearses, spirit boats, or demon-mask escorts.

sentences.zh: 不得朝夕下食。

translations.literal: Do not offer food morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: Do not bring food offerings to the tomb morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 祭奠之法，至於葬，唯清水一杯。

translations.literal: The method of sacrifice: up to burial, only one cup of clear water.
translations.idiomatic: For offerings, up to the time of burial, let there be only one cup of clear water.

sentences.zh: 」子彝奉而行之，州鄉皆稱歎焉。

translations.literal: " His son Yi carried them out, and the province and neighborhood all praised and marveled.
translations.idiomatic: " His son Yi carried out these instructions, and people throughout the province and countryside praised and admired him.

sentences.zh: 阮孝緒

translations.literal: Ruan Xiaoxu
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Xiaoxu

sentences.zh: 阮孝緒字士宗，陳留尉氏人也。

translations.literal: Ruan Xiaoxu, courtesy name Shizong, was a native of Weishi in Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Xiaoxu, courtesy name Shizong, was a native of Weishi in Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 父彥之，宋太尉從事中郎，以清幹流譽。

translations.literal: His father Yanzhi was an Attendant-in-chief in the Secretariat of the Song Grand Commandant, renowned for his integrity and ability.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yanzhi served as Attendant-in-chief in the secretariat of the Song Grand Commandant and was widely praised for his integrity and competence.

sentences.zh: 孝緒七歲出繼從伯胤之，胤之母周氏卒，遺財百餘萬應歸孝緒，孝緒一無所納，盡以歸胤之姊琅邪王晏之母，聞者咸歎異之。

translations.literal: At seven, Xiaoxu was adopted by his father's younger cousin Yinzhi; when Yin's mother Lady Zhou died, a legacy of over a million [coins] should have gone to Xiaoxu, but he accepted nothing and gave it all to Yin's elder sister—the mother of Wang Yan of Langye. All who heard of it sighed in wonder.
translations.idiomatic: At seven, Xiaoxu was adopted by his father's younger cousin Yinzhi. When Yin's mother, Lady Zhou, died, a legacy of more than a million coins should have gone to Xiaoxu, but he accepted none of it and gave it all to Yin's elder sister—the mother of Wang Yan of Langye. All who heard of this marveled.

sentences.zh: 乳人憐其傳重辛苦，輒竊玉羊金獸等物與之。

translations.literal: His wet nurse, pitying his hard lot as heir, secretly stole jade sheep, gold beasts, and other objects and gave them to him.
translations.idiomatic: His wet nurse, pitying the hardship of his role as heir, secretly stole jade sheep, gold beasts, and other valuables and gave them to him.

sentences.zh: 孝緒見而駭愕，啟彥之送還王氏。

translations.literal: Xiaoxu, seeing them, was alarmed and astonished; he informed Yanzhi and sent them back to the Wang family.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaoxu saw them he was shocked; he told Yanzhi and had them returned to the Wang family.

sentences.zh: 幼至孝，性沈靜，雖與童兒遊戲，恒以穿池築山為樂。

translations.literal: From childhood he was filial to the utmost; his nature was quiet and reserved; even when playing with children, he always took delight in digging pools and building hills.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he was deeply filial and quiet by nature; even when playing with other children, he always amused himself by digging ponds and building miniature mountains.

sentences.zh: 年十三，遍通五經。

translations.literal: At thirteen he had thoroughly mastered the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he had mastered all five classics.

sentences.zh: 十五冠而見其父彥之，彥之誡曰：「三加彌尊，人倫之始，宜思自勖，以庇爾躬。

translations.literal: At fifteen he was capped and presented himself to his father Yanzhi, who admonished him: "With each of the three capping rituals one grows more honored— it is the beginning of human relations; you should think on exerting yourself to protect your person.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he was capped and went to see his father Yanzhi, who admonished him: "With each of the three capping ceremonies you grow more honored— this is the beginning of human duty. You should strive to strengthen yourself and safeguard your life.

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「願跡松子於瀛海，追許由於穹穀，庶保促生，以免塵累。

translations.literal: " He replied: "I wish to follow Master Pine to the isles of the eastern sea and pursue Xu You to deep valleys— hoping to keep this brief life intact and escape the dust of worldly entanglements.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied: "I wish to follow Master Pine to the isles of the eastern sea and pursue Xu You into deep mountain valleys, hoping to preserve this brief life and escape the burdens of the world.

sentences.zh: 」自是屏居一室，非定省未嘗出戶，家人莫見其面，親友因呼為居士。

translations.literal: " From then on he secluded himself in one room; except for greeting his parents morning and evening he never left the door; his household barely saw his face; relatives and friends therefore called him "the Recluse."
translations.idiomatic: " From then on he shut himself in a single room; except for the morning and evening greetings owed his parents, he never crossed the threshold. His own household scarcely saw his face, and relatives and friends called him "the Recluse."

sentences.zh: 年十六，父喪不服綿纊，雖蔬菜有味亦吐之。

translations.literal: At sixteen, when his father died, he wore no silk or ramie in mourning; even when vegetables had flavor he would spit them out.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen, when his father died, he wore no silk or ramie in mourning; even when plain vegetables tasted good, he would spit them out.

sentences.zh: 外兄王晏貴顯，屢至其門，孝緒度之必至顛覆，聞其笳管，穿籬逃匿，不與相見。

translations.literal: His maternal cousin Wang Yan became wealthy and eminent and repeatedly came to his door; Xiaoxu judged that Yan would surely come to ruin; hearing his pipes and drums, he would break through the hedge and flee, refusing to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: His maternal cousin Wang Yan rose to wealth and power and came to his door again and again. Xiaoxu judged that Yan would surely come to ruin; whenever he heard Yan's pipes and drums, he would break through the hedge and flee, refusing to meet him.

sentences.zh: 曾食醬美，問之，雲是王家所得，便吐餐覆醬。

translations.literal: Once he ate sauce that tasted fine; on inquiry learning it came from the Wang household, he spat out his meal and overturned the sauce.
translations.idiomatic: Once he ate a sauce that tasted unusually good; when he learned it had come from the Wang household, he spat out his meal and overturned the dish.

sentences.zh: 及晏誅，親戚咸為之懼。

translations.literal: When Yan was executed, kinsmen all feared for him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan was executed, his kinsmen all feared for Xiaoxu as well.

sentences.zh: 孝緒曰：「親而不党，何坐之及。

translations.literal: Xiaoxu said: "One may be related without taking sides— what crime could reach me?
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoxu said: "One may be kin without sharing guilt— what offense could touch me?

sentences.zh: 」竟獲免。

translations.literal: " In the end he escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end he was spared.

sentences.zh: 梁武起兵圍建鄴，家貧無以爨，僮妾竊鄰人墓樵以繼火。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang raised troops and besieged Jiankang, the family was too poor to cook; a servant secretly took firewood from a neighbor's tomb mound to keep the fire going.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Liang raised troops and besieged Jiankang, the family was too poor to cook; a servant secretly took firewood from a neighbor's tomb to keep the fire alive.

sentences.zh: 孝緒知之，乃不食，更令撤屋而炊。

translations.literal: Xiaoxu learned of it and then refused to eat, instead ordering them to dismantle the house for fuel.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaoxu learned of this, he refused to eat and ordered them instead to tear down the house for firewood.

sentences.zh: 所居以一鹿床為精舍，以樹環繞。

translations.literal: Where he lived, a single deer-hide couch served as his retreat, encircled by trees.
translations.idiomatic: He made a single deer-hide couch his dwelling and surrounded it with trees.

sentences.zh: 天監初，御史中丞任昉尋其兄履之，欲造而不敢，望而歎曰：「其室雖邇，其人甚遠。

translations.literal: Early in Tianjian, the Censor-in-chief Ren Fang sought his elder brother Lüzhi and wished to visit [Xiaoxu] but dared not; gazing from afar he sighed: "His dwelling is near, yet the man is far away.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianjian, the Censor-in-chief Ren Fang looked up his elder brother Lüzhi and wished to visit Xiaoxu but did not dare. Gazing from afar he sighed: "His dwelling is close, yet the man himself is far away.

sentences.zh: 」其為名流所欽尚如此。

translations.literal: " Thus was he admired and esteemed by eminent men.
translations.idiomatic: " Such was the esteem in which eminent men held him.

sentences.zh: 自是欽慕風譽者，莫不懷刺斂衽，望塵而息。

translations.literal: From then on all who admired his reputation, without exception, tucked their calling cards, straightened their robes, and halted at sight of his dust.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, all who admired his reputation tucked away their calling cards, straightened their robes, and stopped at the sight of his dust— not daring to approach casually.

sentences.zh: 殷芸欲贈以詩，昉曰：「趣舍既異，何必相干。

translations.literal: Yin Yun wished to present him with a poem; Fang said: "Our inclinations and refusals already differ— why must we impose on one another?
translations.idiomatic: Yin Yun wished to present him with a poem, but Fang said: "Our paths already diverge— why force an encounter?

sentences.zh: 」芸乃止。

translations.literal: " Yin then desisted.
translations.idiomatic: " Yin then gave up the idea.

sentences.zh: 唯與比部郎裴子野交。

translations.literal: He associated only with the Director of the Ministry of Revenue Pei Ziye.
translations.idiomatic: He kept company only with Pei Ziye, Director of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 子野薦之尚書徐勉，言其「年十餘歲隨父為湘州行事，不書官紙，以成親之清白。

translations.literal: Ziye recommended him to the Minister Xu Mian, saying of him: "From his teens when he followed his father as acting governor of Xiangzhou, he would not write on official paper, so as to preserve his father's integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Ziye recommended him to Minister Xu Mian, saying of him: "From his teens, when he accompanied his father as acting governor of Xiangzhou, he refused to write on official paper so as to preserve his father's reputation for integrity.

sentences.zh: 論其志行粗類管幼安，比以采章如似皇甫謐」。

translations.literal: " Judging his aspiration and conduct, he roughly resembles Guan You'an; comparing his literary ornament, he seems like Huangfu Mi."
translations.idiomatic: " In aspiration and conduct he roughly resembles Guan You'an; in literary grace he is much like Huangfu Mi."

sentences.zh: 天監十二年，詔公卿舉士，秘書監傅照上疏薦之，與吳郡範元琰俱征，並不到。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Tianjian, an edict ordered nobles and ministers to recommend scholars; Director of the Secretariat Fu Zhao submitted a memorial recommending him; he and Fan Yuanyan of Wu commandery were both summoned and neither came.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Tianjian, an edict ordered nobles and ministers to recommend scholars. Director of the Secretariat Fu Zhao submitted a memorial recommending him; he and Fan Yuanyan of Wu commandery were both summoned, and neither appeared.

sentences.zh: 陳郡袁峻謂曰：「往者天地閉，賢人隱。

translations.literal: Yuan Jun of Chen commandery said to him: "Formerly when Heaven and Earth were closed, worthies hid away.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Jun of Chen commandery said to him: "In former times, when Heaven and Earth were shut, worthies went into hiding.

sentences.zh: 今世路已清，而子猶遁，可乎？

translations.literal: Now the ways of the age are clear, yet you still withdraw— is that permissible?
translations.idiomatic: Now the age is enlightened, yet you still withdraw— can that be right?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「昔周德雖興，夷、齊不厭薇蕨。

translations.literal: " He replied: "In antiquity, though Zhou virtue rose, Boyi and Shuqi did not tire of bracken and ferns.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied: "In antiquity, though the Zhou dynasty rose, Boyi and Shuqi did not weary of bracken and ferns.

sentences.zh: 漢道方盛，黃、綺無悶山林。

translations.literal: When Han's Way was flourishing, Huang and Qi felt no discontent in mountain forests.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han dynasty was at its height, Huang and Qi felt no discontent in the mountains and forests.

sentences.zh: 為仁由己，何關人世？

translations.literal: Practicing benevolence depends on oneself— what has it to do with the human world?
translations.idiomatic: To practice benevolence is one's own choice— what has that to do with the state of the world?

sentences.zh: 況僕非往賢之類邪？

translations.literal: Moreover, am I truly of the same sort as those ancients?
translations.idiomatic: Besides, am I really the equal of those ancient worthies?

sentences.zh: 」初，謝朏及伏暅應徵，天子以為隱者苟立虛名，以要顯譽，故孝緒與何胤並得遂其高志。

translations.literal: " Earlier, when Xie Tiao and Fu Yong answered summonses, the Son of Heaven judged that recluses who frivolously sought empty fame to gain conspicuous repute [were suspect]; therefore Xiaoxu and He Yin were both able to fulfill their lofty ambitions.
translations.idiomatic: " Earlier, when Xie Tiao and Fu Yong answered imperial summons, the emperor concluded that some recluses merely cultivated empty reputations to win conspicuous praise. For that reason Xiaoxu and He Yin were both allowed to fulfill their lofty aspirations.

sentences.zh: 後於鍾山聽講，母王氏忽有疾，兄弟欲召之。

translations.literal: Later, while lecturing on Zhong Mountain, his mother Lady Wang suddenly fell ill; his brothers wished to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while he was lecturing on Zhong Mountain, his mother Lady Wang suddenly fell ill, and his brothers wanted to send for him.

sentences.zh: 母曰：「孝緒至性冥通，必當自到。

translations.literal: The mother said: "Xiaoxu's supreme nature penetrates the unseen— he is sure to come of himself.
translations.idiomatic: His mother said: "Xiaoxu's filial nature reaches into the unseen— he is sure to come on his own.

sentences.zh: 」果心驚而反，鄰里嗟異之。

translations.literal: " Indeed his heart started and he returned; neighbors marveled and wondered.
translations.idiomatic: " And indeed his heart suddenly stirred and he returned; neighbors marveled at it.

sentences.zh: 合藥須得生人參，舊傳鍾山所出。

translations.literal: Compounding the medicine required fresh ginseng; tradition held it was found on Zhong Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: To prepare the medicine they needed fresh ginseng, which tradition said grew on Zhong Mountain.

sentences.zh: 孝緒躬曆幽險，累日不逢。

translations.literal: Xiaoxu personally traversed deep and perilous places, going many days without finding any.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoxu searched the deep and perilous places himself, going many days without finding any.

sentences.zh: 忽見一鹿前行，孝緒感而隨後，至一所遂滅，就視，果獲此草。

translations.literal: Suddenly he saw a deer going ahead; moved, Xiaoxu followed after; reaching a spot it vanished; going to look, he indeed obtained this herb.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly he saw a deer ahead; moved, Xiaoxu followed it until, at one place, it vanished. He went to look and indeed found the herb.

sentences.zh: 母得服之遂愈，時皆言其孝感所致。

translations.literal: His mother took it and was cured; all said at the time this was due to his filial feeling moving Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: His mother took it and recovered; everyone said at the time that this came of his filial devotion moving Heaven.

sentences.zh: 有善筮者張有道曰：「見子隱跡而心難明，自非考之龜蓍，無以驗也。

translations.literal: A skilled diviner, Zhang Youdao, said: "Seeing you in hidden traces while your heart is hard to discern, unless I consult the tortoise and yarrow stalks, there is no way to verify it.
translations.idiomatic: A skilled diviner named Zhang Youdao said: "I see you living in seclusion, yet your inner mind is hard to read. Unless I consult the tortoise shell and yarrow stalks, there is no way to test it.

sentences.zh: 」及布卦，既揲五爻，曰：「此將為咸，應感之法，非嘉遯之兆。

translations.literal: " When the hexagram was laid out and five lines had been counted, he said: "This will become Xian [Influence]; it is a method of responsive feeling— not an omen of blessed retreat.
translations.idiomatic: " When the hexagram was cast and five lines had been counted, he said: "This will become Xian, Influence— a sign of responsive communion, not an omen of blessed withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 」孝緒曰：「安知後爻不為上九。

translations.literal: " Xiaoxu said: "How do you know the remaining line will not be the top nine?
translations.idiomatic: " Xiaoxu said: "How do you know the final line will not be the top nine?

sentences.zh: 」果成遯卦。

translations.literal: " It indeed became the hexagram Dun [Retreat].
translations.idiomatic: " It indeed became the hexagram Dun, Retreat.

sentences.zh: 有道歎曰：「此所謂'肥遯無不利'，象實應德，心跡並也。

translations.literal: Youdao sighed: "This is what is called 'the fat retreat— nothing unfavorable'; the image truly matches the virtue; inner mind and outward traces align.
translations.idiomatic: Youdao sighed and said: "This is what is meant by 'the well-fed retreat— nothing unfavorable.' The omen truly matches the virtue; mind and conduct are one.

sentences.zh: 」孝緒曰：「雖獲遯卦，而上九爻不發，升遐之道，便當高謝許生。

translations.literal: " Xiaoxu said: "Though I received the Dun hexagram, the top nine line did not activate; the Way of ascending to distant heights— I ought at once to take my leave like Master Xu.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiaoxu said: "Though I received the Dun hexagram, the top nine line did not activate. On the path of ascending to distant heights, I ought at once to take my leave as Xu You did.

sentences.zh: 」乃著高隱傳，上自炎皇，終於天監末，斟酌分為三品：言行超逸，名氏弗傳，為上篇；

translations.literal: " He then authored the Biographies of Lofty Recluses, from the Flame Emperor down to the end of Tianjian, judiciously divided into three grades: words and deeds transcendent, names and clans untransmitted— the upper fascicle;
translations.idiomatic: " He then wrote the Biographies of Lofty Recluses, from the Flame Emperor down to the end of Tianjian, which he judiciously divided into three grades: those whose words and deeds were transcendent but whose names were not preserved— the upper fascicle;

sentences.zh: 始終不耗，姓名可錄，為中篇；

translations.literal: from beginning to end undiminished, names recordable— the middle fascicle;
translations.idiomatic: those whose integrity never waned and whose names could be recorded— the middle fascicle;

sentences.zh: 掛冠人世，棲心塵表，為下篇。

translations.literal: casting off the cap in the human world, lodging the heart beyond the dust— the lower fascicle.
translations.idiomatic: those who hung up their official caps in the human world yet kept their hearts beyond the dust— the lower fascicle.

sentences.zh: 湘東王著忠臣傳，集釋氏碑銘、丹陽尹錄、研神記，並先簡孝緒而後施行。

translations.literal: The Prince of Xiangdong authored Biographies of Loyal Ministers, compiled Buddhist stele inscriptions, Records of the Mayor of Danyang, and Investigations of the Spirit— all were first submitted to Xiaoxu for selection before being implemented.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Xiangdong wrote Biographies of Loyal Ministers and compiled Buddhist stele inscriptions, Records of the Mayor of Danyang, and Investigations of the Spirit; all were first sent to Xiaoxu for review before publication.

sentences.zh: 南平元襄王聞其名，致書要之，不赴，曰：「非志驕富貴，但性畏廟堂，若使麏麚可驂，何以異夫驥騄。」

translations.literal: The Prince of Nanping, Yuan Xiang, hearing his name, sent a letter inviting him; he did not go, saying: "It is not that I scorn wealth and honor in pride; it is simply that by nature I fear the court hall— if roe deer and elk could be yoked as carriage teams, how would that differ from thoroughbreds and piebalds?"
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yuanxiang of Nanping, hearing his name, sent a letter inviting him, but he did not go. He said: "It is not that I disdain wealth and rank out of pride; I am simply by nature afraid of the court. If roe deer and elk could be harnessed as carriage teams, how would that differ from pairing thoroughbreds?"

sentences.zh: 初，建武末，青溪宮東門無故自崩，大風拔東宮門外楊樹，或以問孝緒。

translations.literal: Earlier, near the end of Jianwu, the east gate of Qingxi Palace collapsed for no reason; a great wind uprooted willows outside the Eastern Palace gate; some asked Xiaoxu about it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, near the end of the Jianwu era, the east gate of Qingxi Palace collapsed for no apparent reason, and a great wind uprooted the willows outside the Eastern Palace gate. Some asked Xiaoxu what this meant.

sentences.zh: 孝緒曰：「青溪皇家舊宅，齊為木行，東為木位。

translations.literal: Xiaoxu said: "Qingxi is the former dwelling of the imperial house; Qi belonged to the Wood phase; east is the position of Wood.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoxu said: "Qingxi is the former seat of the imperial house. Qi belonged to the Wood phase, and east is the direction of Wood.

sentences.zh: 今東門自壞，木其衰矣。」

translations.literal: Now the east gate has collapsed of itself— Wood must be in decline."
translations.idiomatic: Now the east gate has collapsed on its own— Wood must be failing."

sentences.zh: 武帝禁畜讖緯，孝緒兼有其書，或勸藏之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu forbade keeping prognostic texts and weft writings; Xiaoxu happened to possess such books; some urged him to hide them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu forbade the keeping of prognostic texts and weft writings; Xiaoxu happened to own such books, and some urged him to conceal them.

sentences.zh: 答曰：「昔劉德重淮南秘要，適為更生之禍，杜瓊所謂不如不知，此言美矣。

translations.literal: He replied: "Formerly Liu De treasured the secret essentials of Huainan— it brought him precisely the disaster of rebirth; what Du Qiong called 'better not to know'— that saying is beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Long ago Liu De treasured the secret writings of Huainan and thereby brought on the disaster of being executed and reburied. As Du Qiong said, 'Better not to know'— that is fine counsel.

sentences.zh: 」客有求之，答曰：「己所不欲，豈可嫁禍於人。

translations.literal: " A guest sought them; he replied: "What I myself do not desire— how could I marry disaster onto another?
translations.idiomatic: " When a guest asked for them, he replied: "What I would not want for myself, how could I pass off as another's misfortune?

sentences.zh: 」乃焚之。

translations.literal: " He then burned them.
translations.idiomatic: " He then burned them.

sentences.zh: 鄱陽忠烈王妃，孝緒姊也。

translations.literal: The Princess of Poyang, the Loyal Martyr, was Xiaoxu's elder sister.
translations.idiomatic: The princess consort of the Loyal Martyr of Poyang was Xiaoxu's elder sister.

sentences.zh: 王嘗命駕欲就之遊，孝緒鑿垣而逃，卒不肯見。

translations.literal: The prince once ordered his carriage to visit him for an outing; Xiaoxu broke through the wall and fled, ultimately refusing to meet.
translations.idiomatic: The prince once ordered his carriage to visit him, but Xiaoxu broke through the wall and fled, refusing to meet him to the end.

sentences.zh: 王悵然歎息。

translations.literal: The prince sighed in desolation.
translations.idiomatic: The prince sighed in disappointment.

sentences.zh: 王諸子篤渭陽之情，歲時之貢，無所受納，未嘗相見，竟不之識。

translations.literal: The prince's sons cherished deep affection as maternal kin; seasonal gifts they never accepted or kept; they never met— in the end they did not even know one another by sight.
translations.idiomatic: The prince's sons cherished the ties of maternal kinship and sent seasonal gifts, but Xiaoxu never accepted them. They never met, and in the end did not even know one another by sight.

sentences.zh: 或問其故，孝緒曰：「我本素賤，不應為王侯姻戚，邂逅所逢，豈關始願。

translations.literal: When someone asked the reason, Xiaoxu said: "I am by origin plain and lowly; I ought not to be kinsman by marriage to princes and marquises— what chance encounter brought was never my original wish.
translations.idiomatic: When someone asked why, Xiaoxu said: "I am by nature plain and lowly; I ought not to be kin by marriage to princes and marquises. What chance brought together was never what I originally wished for.

sentences.zh: 」劉歊曾以米饋之，孝緒不納，歊亦棄之。

translations.literal: " Liu Huan once presented him with rice; Xiaoxu would not accept it, and Huan also discarded it.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Huan once sent him rice as a gift; Xiaoxu would not accept it, and Huan threw it away as well.

sentences.zh: 末年蔬食斷酒，其恒供養石像先有損壞，心欲補之，罄心敬禮，經一夜忽然完復。

translations.literal: In his later years he ate vegetables and abstained from wine. A stone image he had long supplied with worship had earlier been damaged; his heart wished to repair it. He poured out his heart in reverent worship, and after one night it was suddenly restored whole.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he ate only vegetables and abstained from wine. A stone image he had long worshipped had been damaged; wishing to repair it, he poured himself into reverent worship, and after a single night it was suddenly whole again.

sentences.zh: 眾並異之。

translations.literal: All alike marvelled at it.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone marvelled at it.

sentences.zh: 大同二年正月，孝緒自筮卦，「吾壽與劉著作同年」。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Datong, Xiaoxu cast hexagrams for himself: "My lifespan will be the same year as Liu the Compiler."
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year of Datong, Xiaoxu divined for himself and concluded, "My lifespan will end in the same year as Liu the Compiler."

sentences.zh: 及劉杳卒，孝緒曰：「劉侯逝矣，吾其幾何。

translations.literal: When Liu Yao died, Xiaoxu said: "Lord Liu has passed— how much longer have I?
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yao died, Xiaoxu said, "Lord Liu has gone— how much time do I have left?

sentences.zh: 」其年十月卒，年五十八。

translations.literal: " That year in the tenth month he died, aged fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: " That same year, in the tenth month, he died at the age of fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 梁簡文在東宮，隆恩厚贈，子恕等述先志不受。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jianwen of Liang was in the Eastern Palace, he lavished favor and generous posthumous gifts; his sons Shu and the others, stating their father's wishes, did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Jianwen of Liang was crown prince, he heaped honors and generous posthumous gifts upon him, but his sons Shu and the others, citing their father's wishes, declined them.

sentences.zh: 顧協以為恩異常均，議令恭受。

translations.literal: Gu Xie held that the favor was exceptional and even-handed, and proposed that they accept it respectfully.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Xie held that the imperial favor was extraordinary and fairly bestowed, and urged them to accept it with due respect.

sentences.zh: 門徒追論德行，諡曰文貞處士。

translations.literal: His disciples, appraising his conduct and virtue posthumously, gave him the posthumous title Wen Zhen Recluse.
translations.idiomatic: His disciples reviewed his conduct and virtue after his death and gave him the posthumous title Wen Zhen Recluse.

sentences.zh: 所著七錄、削繁等一百八十一卷，並行於世。

translations.literal: His writings, including the Seven Records and Eliminating Redundancy, one hundred eighty-one scrolls in all, all circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His works, including the Seven Records and Eliminating Redundancy—one hundred eighty-one scrolls in all—circulated widely in his day.

sentences.zh: 初，孝緒所撰高隱傳中篇所載一百三十七人，劉歊、劉籲覽其書曰：「昔嵇康所贊，缺一自擬，今四十之數，將待吾等成邪。

translations.literal: Early on, among the one hundred thirty-seven persons recorded in the middle fascicle of the High Recluses that Xiaoxu compiled, Liu Huan and Liu Xu read the book and said: "Long ago what Ji Kang praised was one short of filling out his own count— now with forty persons, are you waiting for us to complete the number?
translations.idiomatic: Early on, among the one hundred thirty-seven figures recorded in the middle fascicle of the High Recluses that Xiaoxu compiled, Liu Huan and Liu Xu read the work and said, "Long ago Ji Kang's roll of praise was one name short of including himself— and now you have forty. Are you waiting for us to fill out the count?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「所謂荀君雖少，後事當付鍾君。

translations.literal: " He replied: "As the saying goes, though Lord Xun was young, later affairs would fall to Lord Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "As the saying goes, though Lord Xun was young, later affairs would be entrusted to Lord Zhong.

sentences.zh: 若素車白馬之日，輒獲麟於二子。

translations.literal: " When the day of the plain carriage and white horses comes, I shall obtain a qilin in the two of you.
translations.idiomatic: " When the day of the plain carriage and white horses arrives, I shall find my qilin in the two of you.

sentences.zh: 」歊、籲果卒，乃益二傳。

translations.literal: " Huan and Xu did indeed die, and he then added two biographies.
translations.idiomatic: " Huan and Xu did indeed die, and he then added two biographies.

sentences.zh: 及孝緒亡，籲兄絜錄其所遺行次篇末，成絕筆之意云。

translations.literal: When Xiaoxu died, Xu's elder brother Jie recorded his remaining conduct at the end of the fascicle, fulfilling his intention to make it his final writing.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiaoxu died, Xu's elder brother Jie recorded his remaining deeds at the end of the fascicle, carrying out his intention to make it his final work.

sentences.zh: 南嶽鄧先生名郁，荊州建平人也。

translations.literal: Master Deng of Mount Heng was named Yu, a native of Jianping in Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Master Deng of Mount Heng was named Yu and came from Jianping in Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 少而不仕，隱居衡山極峻之嶺，立小板屋兩間，足不下山，斷穀三十餘載，唯以澗水服雲母屑，日夜誦大洞經。

translations.literal: From youth he took no office, dwelling in seclusion on the steepest peak of Mount Heng. He built two small plank rooms, never setting foot off the mountain. For more than thirty years he abstained from grain, taking only stream water with powdered mica, day and night reciting the Scripture of the Great Cavern.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he held no office, living in seclusion on the steepest ridge of Mount Heng. He built two small plank huts and never set foot off the mountain. For more than thirty years he abstained from grain, drinking only stream water mixed with powdered mica while reciting the Scripture of the Great Cavern day and night.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝敬信殊篤，為帝合丹，帝不敢服，起五嶽樓貯之供養，道家吉日，躬往禮拜。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang reverenced and trusted him with exceptional devotion. Yu compounded elixir pills for the emperor; the emperor did not dare take them. He built the Five Peaks Tower to store them for worship; on auspicious Daoist days he went in person to pay homage.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang revered and trusted him with exceptional devotion. Yu compounded elixir pills for the emperor, but the emperor did not dare take them. The emperor built the Five Peaks Tower to store them for veneration and, on auspicious Daoist days, went in person to worship there.

sentences.zh: 白日，神仙魏夫人忽來臨降，乘雲而至，從少嫗三十，並著絳紫羅繡褂褲，年皆可十七八許。

translations.literal: One day the immortal Lady Wei suddenly descended to visit, arriving on clouds, with thirty young serving women all dressed in crimson and purple silk embroidered jackets and trousers, each appearing about seventeen or eighteen years old.
translations.idiomatic: One day the immortal Lady Wei suddenly descended to visit, arriving on clouds with thirty young attendants, all dressed in crimson and purple silk-embroidered jackets and trousers and each appearing about seventeen or eighteen years old.

sentences.zh: 色豔桃李，質勝瓊瑤，言語良久，謂郁曰：「君有仙分，所以故來，尋當相候。

translations.literal: Their beauty rivalled peach and plum blossoms, their refinement surpassed fine jade. After speaking at length, she said to Yu: "You bear the portion of an immortal; that is why I have come. Soon I shall await you.
translations.idiomatic: Their beauty rivalled peach and plum blossoms, their refinement surpassed fine jade. After speaking at length, she said to Yu, "You have the makings of an immortal; that is why I have come. I shall await you before long.

sentences.zh: 」至天監十四年，忽見二青鳥悉如鶴大，鼓翼鳴舞，移晷方去。

translations.literal: " By the fourteenth year of Tianjian, he suddenly saw two blue birds, each as large as a crane, beating their wings and dancing and calling; only after the passage of a full watch did they depart.
translations.idiomatic: " By the fourteenth year of Tianjian, he suddenly saw two blue birds, each as large as a crane, beating their wings, calling, and dancing; only after a full watch had passed did they leave.

sentences.zh: 謂弟子等曰：「求之甚勞，得之甚逸。

translations.literal: He told his disciples: "Seeking it is very toilsome; obtaining it is very effortless.
translations.idiomatic: He told his disciples, "The seeking is very toilsome; the obtaining is very effortless.

sentences.zh: 近青鳥既來，期會至矣。

translations.literal: " The blue birds have now come— the appointed meeting has arrived.
translations.idiomatic: " The blue birds have now come— the appointed meeting has arrived.

sentences.zh: 」少日無病而終。

translations.literal: " A few days later he died without illness.
translations.idiomatic: " A few days later he died without illness.

sentences.zh: 山內唯聞香氣，世未嘗有。

translations.literal: Only fragrance was heard within the mountain— the world had never known its like.
translations.idiomatic: Only fragrance was heard within the mountain— the world had never known its like.

sentences.zh: 武帝后令周舍為鄧玄傳，具序其事。

translations.literal: Later the emperor had Zhou She compose a biography of Deng the Sage, setting forth the whole affair in order.
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor had Zhou She compose a biography of Deng the Sage, recounting the whole affair in full.

sentences.zh: 陶弘景

translations.literal: Tao Hongjing
translations.idiomatic: Tao Hongjing

sentences.zh: 陶弘景字通明，丹陽秣陵人也。

translations.literal: Tao Hongjing, courtesy name Tongming, was a native of Moling in Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Hongjing, courtesy name Tongming, was a native of Moling in Danyang.

sentences.zh: 祖隆，王府參軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Long was a staff officer in a princely residence.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Long served as a staff officer in a princely household.

sentences.zh: 父貞，孝昌令。

translations.literal: His father Zhen was magistrate of Xiaochang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhen was magistrate of Xiaochang.

sentences.zh: 初，弘景母郝氏夢兩天人手執香爐來至其所，已而有娠。

translations.literal: At first, Hongjing's mother, née Hao, dreamed that two celestial beings bearing censers in their hands came to her dwelling; thereafter she conceived.
translations.idiomatic: At first, Hongjing's mother, Lady Hao, dreamed that two celestial beings bearing censers in their hands came to where she was; afterward she conceived.

sentences.zh: 以宋孝建三年景申歲夏至日生。

translations.literal: He was born on the summer solstice of the jingshen year, the third year of Xiaojian of Song.
translations.idiomatic: He was born on the summer solstice of the jingshen year, the third year of the Xiaojian era of Song.

sentences.zh: 幼有異操，年四五歲，恒以荻為筆，畫灰中學書。

translations.literal: From childhood he showed unusual conduct. At four or five years old he always used reed stalks for brushes, practicing writing by tracing characters in ash.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he showed unusual character. At four or five he always used reed stalks for brushes, practicing writing by tracing characters in ash.

sentences.zh: 至十歲，得葛洪神仙傳，晝夜研尋，便有養生之志。

translations.literal: By age ten he obtained Ge Hong's Biographies of Immortals and studied it day and night, at once acquiring the resolve to cultivate life.
translations.idiomatic: By the age of ten he obtained Ge Hong's Biographies of Immortals and studied it day and night, at once forming the resolve to cultivate longevity.

sentences.zh: 謂人曰：「仰青雲，睹白日，不覺為遠矣。

translations.literal: He told people: "Looking up at blue clouds and gazing at the white sun, I no longer feel that they are far away.
translations.idiomatic: He told people, "When I look up at blue clouds and gaze at the white sun, I no longer feel that they are far away.

sentences.zh: 」父為妾所害，弘景終身不娶。

translations.literal: " His father was killed by a concubine; Hongjing never married throughout his life.
translations.idiomatic: " His father was killed by a concubine, and Hongjing never married for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 及長，身長七尺七寸，神儀明秀，朗目疏眉，細形長額聳耳，耳孔各有十餘毛出外二寸許，右膝有數十黑子作七星文。

translations.literal: When grown, he stood seven feet seven inches tall, with bright and refined bearing, clear eyes and sparse brows, a slender frame, a long forehead, and prominent ears— from each ear canal more than ten hairs protruded outward about two inches; on his right knee were several dozen black marks forming the pattern of the Seven Stars.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up, he stood seven feet seven inches tall, with bright and refined bearing, clear eyes and sparse brows, a slender frame, a long forehead, and prominent ears— from each ear canal more than ten hairs protruded about two inches; on his right knee were several dozen black marks forming the pattern of the Seven Stars.

sentences.zh: 讀書萬餘卷，一事不知，以為深恥。

translations.literal: He read more than ten thousand scrolls; not knowing a single thing he regarded as deep shame.
translations.idiomatic: He read more than ten thousand scrolls and regarded not knowing even one thing as a deep shame.

sentences.zh: 善琴棋，工草隸。

translations.literal: He was skilled at the zither and chess, and accomplished in cursive and clerical scripts.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at the zither and chess and accomplished in cursive and clerical calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 未弱冠，齊高帝作相，引為諸王侍讀，除奉朝請。

translations.literal: Before reaching the capping age, when Emperor Gao of Qi served as chief minister, he was summoned as tutor-reader to the princes and appointed Gentleman Attendant at Court.
translations.idiomatic: Before he came of age, when Emperor Gao of Qi was chief minister, he was summoned as tutor-reader to the princes and appointed Gentleman Attendant at Court.

sentences.zh: 雖在朱門，閉影不交外物，唯以披閱為務。

translations.literal: Though he dwelt in the vermilion gates, he shut himself away and mingled with nothing outside, devoting himself solely to reading.
translations.idiomatic: Though he lived within the vermilion gates of power, he kept to himself and mingled with nothing outside, devoting himself solely to reading.

sentences.zh: 朝儀故事，多所取焉。

translations.literal: From court ritual and precedent he drew much that he used.
translations.idiomatic: From court ritual and precedent he drew much of what he used.

sentences.zh: 家貧，求宰縣不遂。

translations.literal: His family was poor; he sought a magistracy of a county but did not obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: His family was poor, and his bid for a county magistracy went nowhere.

sentences.zh: 永明十年，脫朝服掛神武門，上表辭祿。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yongming he removed his court robes and hung them at the Shenwu Gate, submitting a memorial to resign his salary.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Yongming he removed his court robes, hung them at the Shenwu Gate, and submitted a memorial resigning his stipend.

sentences.zh: 詔許之，賜以束帛，敕所在月給伏苓五斤，白蜜二升，以供服餌。

translations.literal: An edict approved it and granted him silk bolts; he was ordered to receive monthly from his locality five jin of poria and two sheng of white honey for his regimen of ingestion.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved his request and granted him bolts of silk; he was ordered to receive five jin of poria and two sheng of white honey each month from his locality for his regimen.

sentences.zh: 及發，公卿祖之征虜亭，供帳甚盛，車馬填咽，咸雲宋、齊以來未有斯事。

translations.literal: When he departed, ministers and high officials saw him off at the Campaign-against-Barbarians Pavilion; the provisioning of tents was very lavish, carriages and horses choked the road—all said that since Song and Qi there had never been such an event.
translations.idiomatic: When he set out, ministers and high officials saw him off at the Campaign-against-Barbarians Pavilion; the tents and provisions were lavish, and carriages and horses choked the road—all said that since Song and Qi there had never been such a send-off.

sentences.zh: 於是止于句容之句曲山。

translations.literal: Thereupon he settled on Mount Gouqu in Jurong.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he settled on Mount Gouqu in Jurong.

sentences.zh: 恒曰：「此山下是第八洞宮，名金壇華陽之天，周回一百五十里。

translations.literal: He always said: "Below this mountain is the Eighth Grotto-Palace, called the Heaven of the Golden Altar and Flourishing Yang, circling one hundred fifty li in circumference.
translations.idiomatic: He always said, "Below this mountain lies the Eighth Grotto-Palace, called the Heaven of the Golden Altar and Flourishing Yang, circling one hundred fifty li in circumference.

sentences.zh: 昔漢有咸陽三茅君得道來掌此山，故謂之茅山。

translations.literal: " In Han times the Three Lords Mao of Xianyang attained the Way and came to oversee this mountain; that is why it is called Mount Mao.
translations.idiomatic: " In Han times the Three Lords Mao of Xianyang attained the Way and came to oversee this mountain; that is why it is called Mount Mao.

sentences.zh: 」乃中山立館，自號華陽陶隱居。

translations.literal: " He then built a lodge midway up the mountain and styled himself Tao the Hermit of Huayang.
translations.idiomatic: " He then built a lodge midway up the mountain and styled himself Tao the Hermit of Huayang.

sentences.zh: 人間書劄，即以隱居代名。

translations.literal: In worldly letters he used Hermit in place of his name.
translations.idiomatic: In worldly correspondence he used Hermit in place of his personal name.
