sentences.zh: 始從東陽孫游岳受符圖經法，遍曆名山，尋訪仙藥。

translations.literal: At first he received talisman charts and scripture methods from Sun Youyue of Dongyang, travelling all famous mountains to seek out immortal herbs.
translations.idiomatic: At first he received talisman charts and scripture methods from Sun Youyue of Dongyang, then travelled through all the famous mountains seeking immortal herbs.

sentences.zh: 身既輕捷，性愛山水，每經澗穀，必坐臥其間，吟詠盤桓，不能已已。

translations.literal: His body was already light and nimble, and by nature he loved mountains and streams; whenever he passed through brooks and valleys he had to sit or lie among them, chanting and lingering, unable to tear himself away.
translations.idiomatic: His body was already light and nimble, and by nature he loved mountains and streams; whenever he passed through brooks and valleys he had to sit or lie among them, chanting and lingering, unable to pull himself away.

sentences.zh: 謂門人曰：「吾見朱門廣廈，雖識其華樂，而無欲往之心。

translations.literal: He told his disciples: "When I see vermilion gates and broad mansions, though I recognize their splendor and pleasure, I have no wish to go there.
translations.idiomatic: He told his disciples, "When I see vermilion gates and broad mansions, though I recognize their splendor and pleasure, I have no wish to go there.

sentences.zh: 望高岩，瞰大澤，知此難立止，自恒欲就之。

translations.literal: " Gazing at high cliffs and looking down on great marshes, I know how hard it is to stay still—I always long to go to them.
translations.idiomatic: " When I gaze at high cliffs and look down on great marshes, I know how hard it is to stay still—I always long to go to them.

sentences.zh: 且永明中求祿，得輒差舛；

translations.literal: " Moreover, when I sought salary in the Yongming era, what I obtained was always awry;
translations.idiomatic: " Moreover, when I sought office in the Yongming era, what I obtained was always awry;

sentences.zh: 若不爾，豈得為今日之事。

translations.literal: " if it had not been so, how could I have achieved what I have today?
translations.idiomatic: " if it had not been so, how could I have achieved what I have today?

sentences.zh: 豈唯身有仙相，亦緣勢使之然。

translations.literal: " Is it not only that my body bears the marks of immortality, but also that circumstance made it so?
translations.idiomatic: " Is it not only that my body bears the marks of immortality, but also that circumstance made it so?

sentences.zh: 」沈約為東陽郡守，高其志節，累書要之，不至。

translations.literal: " When Shen Yue was governor of Dongyang, he esteemed his resolve and integrity and repeatedly sent letters inviting him, but Hongjing did not come.
translations.idiomatic: " When Shen Yue was governor of Dongyang, he admired his resolve and integrity and repeatedly sent letters inviting him, but Hongjing never came.

sentences.zh: 弘景為人員通謙謹，出處冥會，心如明鏡，遇物便了。

translations.literal: Hongjing as a man was broadly adaptable, modest, and careful; in advance and retreat he accorded with hidden design; his mind was like a bright mirror— encountering things he grasped them at once.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjing was broadly adaptable, modest, and careful; in advance and retreat he moved in accord with hidden design; his mind was like a bright mirror— encountering things, he grasped them at once.

sentences.zh: 言無煩舛，有亦隨覺。

translations.literal: His speech had no troublesome errors; if there were any, he corrected them immediately.
translations.idiomatic: His speech had no troublesome errors; if any arose, he corrected them at once.

sentences.zh: 永元初，更築三層樓，弘景處其上，弟子居其中，賓客至其下。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yongyuan era he built a three-storey tower anew: Hongjing lived on the top, his disciples in the middle, and guests came only to the bottom.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yongyuan era he built a new three-storey tower: Hongjing lived on the top, his disciples in the middle, and guests came only to the bottom.

sentences.zh: 與物遂絕，唯一家僮得至其所。

translations.literal: He was thus cut off from the world; only one household servant could reach where he was.
translations.idiomatic: He was thus cut off from the world; only one household servant could reach where he lived.

sentences.zh: 本便馬善射，晚皆不為，唯聽吹笙而已。

translations.literal: Originally he was adept at horsemanship and archery, but in his later years he did neither, listening only to the playing of the sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Originally he was adept at horsemanship and archery, but in his later years he did neither, listening only to the sheng.

sentences.zh: 特愛松風，庭院皆植松，每聞其響，欣然為樂。

translations.literal: He especially loved the wind in the pines; he planted pines throughout the courtyard, and whenever he heard their sound he took delight in it with pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: He especially loved the wind in the pines; he planted pines throughout the courtyard, and whenever he heard their sound he took quiet delight in it.

sentences.zh: 有時獨游泉石，望見者以為仙人。

translations.literal: At times he wandered alone among springs and rocks; those who saw him took him for an immortal.
translations.idiomatic: At times he wandered alone among springs and rocks, and those who saw him took him for an immortal.

sentences.zh: 性好著述，尚奇異，顧惜光景，老而彌篤。

translations.literal: By nature he loved writing, valued the strange and extraordinary, cherished the light of day, and in old age became all the more devoted.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he loved writing, valued the strange and extraordinary, cherished the light of day, and in old age became all the more devoted to his work.

sentences.zh: 尤明陰陽五行、風角星算、山川地理、方圖產物、醫術本草，著帝代年曆，以算推知漢熹平三年丁丑冬至，加時在日中，而天實以乙亥冬至，加時在夜半，凡差三十八刻，是漢曆後天二日十二刻也。

translations.literal: He was especially versed in yin-yang and the five phases, wind horns, star calculation, mountains, rivers, and geography, regional maps and local products, medical arts and materia medica. He wrote An Imperial Chronology; by calculation he deduced that at the winter solstice of the third year of Xiping of Han, in the dingchou year, the added hour fell at midday— whereas Heaven in fact had yihai for the winter solstice, with the added hour at midnight; the total discrepancy was thirty-eight quarters of an hour. Thus the Han calendar was two days and twelve quarters behind Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially versed in yin-yang and the five phases, wind horns, star calculation, mountains, rivers, and geography, regional maps and local products, medical arts and materia medica. He wrote An Imperial Chronology and, by calculation, determined that at the winter solstice of the third year of Xiping of Han, in the dingchou year, the added hour fell at midday— whereas Heaven in fact placed the winter solstice in yihai with the added hour at midnight; the total discrepancy was thirty-eight quarters of an hour. Thus the Han calendar lagged Heaven by two days and twelve quarters.

sentences.zh: 又以歷代皆取其先妣母后配饗地只，以為神理宜然，碩學通儒，咸所不悟。

translations.literal: He also held that every dynasty took its deceased mothers and empresses to share sacrifice with Earth Spirit, believing this conformed to divine principle— a point eminent scholars and broadly learned Confucians all failed to grasp.
translations.idiomatic: He also held that every dynasty took its deceased mothers and empresses to share sacrifice with the Earth Spirit, believing this conformed to divine principle— a point eminent scholars and broadly learned Confucians all failed to grasp.

sentences.zh: 又嘗造渾天象，高三尺許，地居中央，天轉而地不動，以機動之，悉與天相會。

translations.literal: He also once made an armillary sphere model three feet or so high, with Earth at the center; Heaven revolved while Earth did not move—a mechanism drove it, and everything accorded with Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He also once made an armillary sphere model about three feet high, with Earth at the center; Heaven revolved while Earth remained still—a mechanism drove it, and everything accorded with the heavens.

sentences.zh: 云：「修道所須，非止史官是用」。

translations.literal: He said: "What cultivation of the Way requires is not merely what the historiographers use."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "What the cultivation of the Way requires is not merely what the historiographers use."

sentences.zh: 深慕張良為人，云：「古賢無比」。

translations.literal: He deeply admired Zhang Liang as a man and said: "Among the ancients there is none to compare."
translations.idiomatic: He deeply admired Zhang Liang as a man and said, "Among the ancients there is none to compare."

sentences.zh: 弘景既得神符秘訣，以為神丹可成，而苦無藥物。

translations.literal: Once Hongjing had obtained divine talismans and secret formulas, he believed the divine elixir could be perfected, but he suffered from lack of ingredients.
translations.idiomatic: Once Hongjing had obtained divine talismans and secret formulas, he believed the divine elixir could be perfected, but he lacked the necessary ingredients.

sentences.zh: 帝給黃金、朱砂、曾青、雄黃等。

translations.literal: The emperor supplied gold, cinnabar, azure malachite, realgar, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor supplied gold, cinnabar, azure malachite, realgar, and the like.

sentences.zh: 後合飛丹，色如霜雪，服之體輕。

translations.literal: Later he compounded flying elixir, colored like frost and snow; upon taking it the body grew light.
translations.idiomatic: Later he compounded flying elixir, white as frost and snow; upon taking it the body grew light.

sentences.zh: 及帝服飛丹有驗，益敬重之。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the flying elixir with verified effect, he honored Hongjing all the more.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the flying elixir with verified effect, he honored Hongjing all the more.

sentences.zh: 每得其書，燒香虔受。

translations.literal: Whenever he received a letter from him, he burned incense and reverently accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he received a letter from him, he burned incense and received it with reverence.

sentences.zh: 帝使造年曆，至己巳歲而加朱點，實太清三年也。

translations.literal: The emperor had him compile a calendar; when it reached the jisi year he added a vermilion dot—it was in fact the third year of Taiqing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had him compile a calendar; when it reached the jisi year he added a vermilion dot—it was in fact the third year of Taiqing.

sentences.zh: 帝手敕招之，錫以鹿皮巾。

translations.literal: The emperor personally wrote an edict summoning him and bestowed on him a deer's-hide cap.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally wrote an edict summoning him and bestowed on him a deer's-hide cap.

sentences.zh: 後屢加禮聘，並不出，唯畫作兩牛，一牛散放水草之間，一牛著金籠頭，有人執繩，以杖驅之。

translations.literal: Later he repeatedly increased ritual invitations, but Hongjing never came out; he only painted two oxen— one turned loose among water and grass, one wearing a golden halter with a man holding the rope and driving it with a staff.
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor repeatedly increased ritual invitations, but Hongjing never came out; he only painted two oxen— one turned loose among water and grass, one wearing a golden halter with a man holding the rope and driving it with a staff.

sentences.zh: 武帝笑曰：「此人無所不作，欲學曳尾之龜，豈有可致之理。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu laughed and said: "This man can do anything; he wants to imitate the turtle that drags its tail in the mud—is there any principle by which he can be brought here?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu laughed and said, "This man can do anything; he wants to imitate the turtle that drags its tail in the mud—is there any way he can be brought here?

sentences.zh: 」國家每有吉凶征討大事，無不前以諮詢。

translations.literal: " Whenever the state faced matters of fortune or misfortune, campaigns or great affairs, without fail they first consulted him beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: " Whenever the state faced matters of fortune or misfortune, campaigns or great affairs, without fail they consulted him first.

sentences.zh: 月中常有數信，時人謂為山中宰相。

translations.literal: Several letters each month were regular; people of the time called him the chancellor of the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Several letters each month were regular, and people of the time called him the chancellor of the mountains.

sentences.zh: 二宮及公王貴要參候相繼，贈遺未嘗脫時。

translations.literal: The two palaces and princes, dukes, and important persons paid visits one after another; gifts and presents never ceased for a moment.
translations.idiomatic: The two palaces and princes, dukes, and important persons paid visits one after another; gifts and presents never ceased for a moment.

sentences.zh: 多不納受，縱留者即作功德。

translations.literal: Most he did not accept; whatever he did keep he used for meritorious acts.
translations.idiomatic: Most he did not accept; whatever he did keep he used for meritorious works.

sentences.zh: 天監四年，移居積金東澗。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianjian he moved his residence to Jijin East Stream.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianjian he moved his residence to Jijin East Stream.

sentences.zh: 弘景善辟穀導引之法，自隱處四十許年，年逾八十而有壯容。

translations.literal: Hongjing was skilled in grain-abstaining regimen and daoyin exercises; from his retirement about forty years, past eighty he still had a vigorous countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjing was skilled in grain-abstaining regimen and daoyin exercises; from his retirement for about forty years, past eighty he still had a vigorous countenance.

sentences.zh: 仙書云：「眼方者壽千歲。

translations.literal: Immortal writings say: "Those whose eyes are square live a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: Immortal writings say, "Those whose eyes are square live a thousand years.

sentences.zh: 」弘景末年一眼有時而方。

translations.literal: " In Hongjing's later years one eye was sometimes square.
translations.idiomatic: " In Hongjing's later years one eye was sometimes square.

sentences.zh: 曾夢佛授其菩提記雲，名為勝力菩薩。

translations.literal: He once dreamed that the Buddha granted him the Record of Bodhi, naming him the Bodhisattva Victorious Power.
translations.idiomatic: He once dreamed that the Buddha granted him the Record of Bodhi, naming him the Bodhisattva Victorious Power.

sentences.zh: 乃詣鄮縣阿育王塔自誓，受五大戒。

translations.literal: Thereupon he went to the Ashoka Pagoda in Yin County to vow himself and received the five major precepts.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he went to the Ashoka Pagoda in Yin County to vow himself and received the five major precepts.

sentences.zh: 後簡文臨南徐州，欽其風素，召至後堂，以葛巾進見，與談論數日而去，簡文甚敬異之。

translations.literal: Later when Jianwen held office at Southern Xuzhou, he admired his character and simplicity, summoned him to the rear hall, received him wearing a hemp headcloth, and after several days of conversation sent him away— Jianwen held him in deep esteem and wonder.
translations.idiomatic: Later when Jianwen held office at Southern Xuzhou, he admired his character and simplicity, summoned him to the rear hall, received him wearing a hemp headcloth, and after several days of conversation sent him away— Jianwen held him in deep esteem and wonder.

sentences.zh: 天監中，獻丹于武帝。

translations.literal: During the Tianjian era he presented elixir to Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianjian era he presented elixir to Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 中大通初，又獻二刀，其一名善勝，一名威勝，並為佳寶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhongdatong he again presented two swords, one named Good Victory and one named Awesome Victory, both treasured blades.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhongdatong he again presented two swords, one named Good Victory and one named Awesome Victory, both treasured blades.

sentences.zh: 無疾，自知應逝，逆克亡日，仍為告逝詩。

translations.literal: Without illness, knowing he was due to depart, he calculated in advance the day of death and even composed a farewell poem announcing his demise.
translations.idiomatic: Without illness, knowing he was due to depart, he calculated in advance the day of his death and even composed a farewell poem announcing his demise.

sentences.zh: 大同二年卒，時年八十一。

translations.literal: In the second year of Datong he died, aged eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Datong he died at the age of eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 顏色不變，屈申如常，香氣累日，氛氳滿山。

translations.literal: His complexion did not change; bending and stretching were as usual; fragrance lingered for days, wafting thick through the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: His complexion did not change; bending and stretching were as usual; fragrance lingered for days, wafting thick through the mountain.

sentences.zh: 遺令：「既沒不須沐浴，不須施床，止兩重席於地，因所著舊衣，上加生褲裙及臂衣靺冠巾法服。

translations.literal: His final instructions: "Once I am gone, no bathing is needed, no couch required— only lay two layers of matting on the ground; over the old clothes I am wearing, add fresh trousers, skirt, sleeve-garments, felt cap, headcloth, and ritual vestments.
translations.idiomatic: His final instructions: "Once I am gone, no bathing is needed and no couch required— only lay two layers of matting on the ground; over the old clothes I am wearing, add fresh trousers, skirt, sleeve-garments, felt cap, headcloth, and ritual vestments.

sentences.zh: 左肘錄鈴，右肘藥鈴，佩符絡左腋下。

translations.literal: " At the left elbow a scripture bell, at the right elbow a medicine bell; wear talismans strung at the left armpit.
translations.idiomatic: " Place a scripture bell at the left elbow and a medicine bell at the right elbow; wear talismans strung at the left armpit.

sentences.zh: 繞腰穿環結於前，釵符於髻上。

translations.literal: " Wrap around the waist, thread through rings, and knot in front; pin talismans on the hair knot.
translations.idiomatic: " Wrap around the waist, thread through rings, and knot in front; pin talismans on the hair knot.

sentences.zh: 通以大袈裟覆衾蒙首足。

translations.literal: " Cover entirely with a great kasaya robe as quilt, veiling head and feet.
translations.idiomatic: " Cover entirely with a great kasaya robe as a quilt, veiling head and feet.

sentences.zh: 明器有車馬。

translations.literal: " Grave goods shall include chariots and horses.
translations.idiomatic: " Include chariots and horses among the burial objects.

sentences.zh: 道人道士並在門中，道人左，道士右。

translations.literal: " Lay Daoist adepts and ordained Daoist priests shall both stand within the gate— adepts on the left, priests on the right.
translations.idiomatic: " Place both lay Daoists and ordained priests inside the gate, with lay adepts on the left and priests on the right.

sentences.zh: 百日內夜常然燈，旦常香火。

translations.literal: " Within a hundred days, keep lamps burning through the nights and incense going each morning.
translations.idiomatic: " For a hundred days, burn lamps every night and incense every morning.

sentences.zh: 」弟子遵而行之。

translations.literal: " His disciples obeyed and carried it out.
translations.idiomatic: " His disciples followed these instructions to the letter.

sentences.zh: 詔贈太中大夫，諡曰貞白先生。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously granted him Grand Master of the Palace and conferred the posthumous title Master Zhenbai.
translations.idiomatic: By edict he was posthumously made Grand Master of the Palace, with the posthumous title Master Zhenbai.

sentences.zh: 弘景妙解術數，逆知梁祚覆沒，預製詩云：「夷甫任散誕，平叔坐論空。

translations.literal: Hongjing was deeply skilled in numerology and prognostication; foreknowing the Liang dynasty's ruin, he composed a poem in advance, saying: "Yifu trusted in careless abandon, Pingshu sat discoursing on emptiness.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjing had a profound grasp of numerology and divination. Anticipating the fall of the Liang, he wrote a prophetic poem: "Yifu indulged recklessness and release; Pingshu sat debating the void.

sentences.zh: 豈悟昭陽殿，遂作單于宮。

translations.literal: Who could have guessed Zhaoyang Hall would become the Xiongnu chieftain's palace?
translations.idiomatic: Who dreamed that Zhaoyang Hall would turn into a barbarian ruler's court?

sentences.zh: 」詩秘在篋裏，化後，門人方稍出之。

translations.literal: " The poem he kept secret in a chest; only after his ascension did his disciples gradually bring it forth.
translations.idiomatic: " He kept the poem hidden in a casket, and only after his death did his disciples slowly release it.

sentences.zh: 大同末，人士競談玄理，不習武事，後侯景篡，果在昭陽殿。

translations.literal: At the end of Datong, gentlemen vied to discuss arcane philosophy and neglected military affairs; later Hou Jing usurped power, and it indeed came to pass at Zhaoyang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the final years of Datong, scholars competed in talk of abstruse doctrine while ignoring martial training; when Hou Jing seized power afterward, the prophecy was fulfilled precisely at Zhaoyang Hall.

sentences.zh: 初，弘景母夢青龍無尾，自己升天，弘景果不妻無子。

translations.literal: Earlier, Hongjing's mother dreamed of a green dragon without a tail that ascended heaven from her own body; Hongjing indeed never married and had no children.
translations.idiomatic: Once, Hongjing's mother dreamed of a tailless azure dragon rising to heaven from her own person; Hongjing in fact never took a wife and left no sons.

sentences.zh: 從兄以子松喬嗣。

translations.literal: A cousin male-line adopted his nephew Song Qiao as heir.
translations.idiomatic: A patrilateral cousin adopted his nephew Song Qiao to continue the line.

sentences.zh: 所著學苑百卷，孝經、論語集注、帝代年曆、本草集注、效驗方、肘後百一方、古今州郡記、圖像集要及玉匱記、七曜新舊術疏、占候、合丹法式，共秘密不傳，及撰而未訖又十部，唯弟子得之。

translations.literal: His writings included the Hundred Fascicles of the Academy of Learning, collected commentaries on the Classic of Filial Piety and Analects, dynastic chronologies, a collected commentary on the Materia Medica, verified prescriptions, the Hundred Recipes from the Elbow, records of commanderies ancient and modern, essentials of illustrated compendia, and the Jade Casket Record, new and old treatises on the seven luminaries, prognostication, and alchemical formulas— all kept secret and not transmitted; and ten further works he drafted but did not finish— only his disciples received them.
translations.idiomatic: He authored the Hundred Fascicles of the Academy of Learning, commentaries on the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects, dynastic chronologies, a commentary on the Materia Medica, effective prescriptions, the Hundred Recipes from the Elbow, gazetteers of ancient and modern prefectures, illustrated compendia, the Jade Casket Record, treatises old and new on the seven luminaries, divination manuals, and alchemical formulas— all withheld from circulation— as well as ten unfinished works. Only his disciples ever obtained them.

sentences.zh: 靈和寺沙門釋寶亮欲以納被遺之，未及有言，寶志忽來牽被而去。

translations.literal: The monk Shi Baoliang of Linghe Temple wished to leave him a quilted cotton coverlet as a gift but had not yet spoken when Baozhi suddenly came, pulled the coverlet away, and left.
translations.idiomatic: Baoliang, a monk of Linghe Temple, meant to give him a padded quilt but had not yet said so when Baozhi suddenly appeared, snatched the quilt, and walked off.

sentences.zh: 蔡仲熊嘗問仕何所至。

translations.literal: Cai Zhongxiong once asked how far he would rise in office.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Zhongxiong once asked how high he would climb in his official career.

sentences.zh: 了自不答，直解杖頭左索繩擲與之，莫之解。

translations.literal: Liaozi made no reply; he simply unfastened a rope from the left side of his staff and threw it to him— no one understood it.
translations.idiomatic: Without answering, Liaozi took a rope tied to the left of his staff and tossed it to him; nobody could make sense of it.

sentences.zh: 仲熊至尚書左丞，方知言驗。

translations.literal: When Zhongxiong reached Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, he finally knew the words had been fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: Only when Zhongxiong became Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing did he realize the prophecy had come true.

sentences.zh: 永明中，住東宮後堂，從平旦門中出入。

translations.literal: During Yongming he dwelt in the Eastern Palace rear hall, entering and leaving through the Pingdan Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongming era he lived in the rear hall of the Eastern Palace and passed in and out through Pingdan Gate.

sentences.zh: 末年忽云：「門上血污衣」，褰裳走過。

translations.literal: In his final years he suddenly cried: "Blood on the gate will stain the clothes," and lifting his robe, hurried past.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of his life he suddenly exclaimed, "Blood on the gate will stain one's garments," then hitched up his robe and rushed past.

sentences.zh: 至郁林見害，果以犢車載屍出自此門，舍故閹人徐龍駒宅，而帝頸血流於門限焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yulin was murdered, indeed a bullock cart carried the corpse out through this gate; it stopped at the house of the former eunuch Xu Longju, and the emperor's blood from his neck streamed onto the gate-sill.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yulin was killed, a bullock cart carrying his corpse indeed passed out through this very gate and halted at the house of the former eunuch Xu Longju, and the emperor's blood ran from his neck onto the gate threshold.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝尤深敬事，嘗問年祚遠近。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang held him in deepest reverence; he once asked how near or far his reign's span would be.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang revered him above all and once asked how long his dynasty would endure.

sentences.zh: 答曰：「元嘉元嘉。

translations.literal: He answered: "Yuánjiā, Yuánjiā.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Yuánjiā, Yuánjiā.

sentences.zh: 」帝欣然，以為享祚倍宋文之年。

translations.literal: " The emperor was delighted, taking it to mean his reign would double the years of Emperor Wen of Song.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was pleased, interpreting the phrase to mean he would reign twice as long as Emperor Wen of Song.

sentences.zh: 雖剃鬚髮而常冠帽，下裙納袍，故俗呼為志公。

translations.literal: Though shaven of beard and hair he always wore cap and hat, skirt and robe— hence the common nickname Master Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Although tonsured, he habitually wore cap and hat with skirt and robe, which is why people called him Master Zhi.

sentences.zh: 好為讖記，所謂志公符是也。

translations.literal: He liked to produce prophetic records— the so-called Talismans of Master Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: He was fond of writing prophecy scrolls, known as the Talismans of Master Zhi.

sentences.zh: 高麗聞之，遣使齎綿帽供養。

translations.literal: Goguryeo heard of this and sent envoys bearing padded caps as offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of him, Goguryeo dispatched envoys with padded caps as tribute offerings.

sentences.zh: 天監十三年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the thirteenth year of Tianjian.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirteenth year of Tianjian.

sentences.zh: 將死，忽移寺金剛像出置戶外，語人云：「菩薩當去。

translations.literal: As death approached, he suddenly moved the temple's vajra image outdoors and told people: "The bodhisattva is about to leave.
translations.idiomatic: When he was nearing death, he abruptly had the temple's vajra statue moved outside and told those present, "The bodhisattva is departing.

sentences.zh: 」旬日無疾而終。

translations.literal: " Within ten days he died without illness.
translations.idiomatic: " Ten days later he passed away, with no prior sickness.

sentences.zh: 先是琅邪王筠至莊嚴寺，寶志遇之，與交言歡飲。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wang Yun of Langye came to Zhuangyan Temple; Baozhi met him and they conversed joyfully over drink.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Wang Yun of Langye visited Zhuangyan Temple, where Baozhi joined him in cheerful conversation and wine.

sentences.zh: 至亡，敕命筠為碑，蓋先覺也。

translations.literal: Upon his death, an edict ordered Yun to compose the stele inscription— a mark of foreknowledge.
translations.idiomatic: When Baozhi died, the emperor commanded Yun to write his epitaph— he had seen it coming.

sentences.zh: 諸葛璩

translations.literal: Zhuge Qu
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Qu

sentences.zh: 諸葛璩字幼玫，琅邪陽都人也。

translations.literal: Zhuge Qu, courtesy name Youmei, was a native of Yangdu in Langye.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Qu, style name Youmei, came from Yangdu in Langye.

sentences.zh: 世居京口。

translations.literal: His family had long lived at Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: For generations his family resided at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 璩幼事征士關康之，博涉經史。

translations.literal: In youth Qu studied under the recluse Guan Kangzhi and ranged broadly through the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he studied with the recluse Guan Kangzhi and mastered a wide range of classical and historical texts.

sentences.zh: 復師征士臧榮緒，榮緒著晉書，稱璩有發擿之功，方之壺遂。

translations.literal: He later took as teacher the recluse Zang Rongxu; in his History of Jin Rongxu praised Qu for discoveries and expositions, comparing him to Hu Sui.
translations.idiomatic: He later studied under the recluse Zang Rongxu, who in his History of Jin praised Qu's talent for uncovering hidden facts, likening him to Hu Sui.

sentences.zh: 齊建武初，南徐州行事江祀薦璩於明帝，言璩安貧守道，悅禮敦詩，如其簡退，可揚清厲俗，請辟為議曹從事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwu in Qi, Jiang Si, acting administrator of Southern Xuzhou, recommended Qu to Emperor Ming, saying Qu kept to poverty yet held to the Way, delighted in ritual and honored poetry, and that given his modest retirement he could uplift pure standards and reform custom— he asked that Qu be appointed Attendant of the Discussion Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianwu era of Qi, Jiang Si, acting for Southern Xuzhou, recommended Qu to Emperor Ming, praising his contented poverty, moral steadfastness, love of ritual, and devotion to poetry; deeming such self-effacing integrity fit to ennoble public morals, he asked that Qu be summoned as Attendant of the Discussion Bureau.

sentences.zh: 帝許之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted the request.

sentences.zh: 璩辭不赴。

translations.literal: Qu declined and did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: Qu refused the appointment and did not go.

sentences.zh: 陳郡謝朓為東海太守，下教揚其風概，餉穀百斛。

translations.literal: Xie Tiao of Chen commandery, as Administrator of Donghai, issued an edict commending his character and sent him a hundred hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: When Xie Tiao of Chen commandery served as Administrator of Donghai, he issued a proclamation praising Qu's moral bearing and sent him a hundred hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 梁天監中，舉秀才，不就。

translations.literal: During Liang Tianjian, nominated as xiucai, he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Liang, during Tianjian, he was nominated as a xiucai but declined to serve.

sentences.zh: 璩性勤於誨誘，後生就學者日至。

translations.literal: Qu was diligent in instruction and guidance; young students came daily to study.
translations.idiomatic: Qu devoted himself tirelessly to teaching, and young scholars arrived each day to study with him.

sentences.zh: 居宅狹陋，無以容之。

translations.literal: His dwelling was cramped and could not hold them all.
translations.idiomatic: His home was too narrow and shabby to accommodate them.

sentences.zh: 太守張友為起講舍。

translations.literal: The Administrator Zhang You built a lecture hall for him.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect Zhang You erected a lecture hall for him.

sentences.zh: 璩處身清正，妻子不見喜慍之色，旦夕孜孜，講誦不輟，時人益以此宗之。

translations.literal: Qu conducted himself with pure integrity; wife and children never saw joy or anger on his face; morning and evening he applied himself tirelessly, lecturing and reciting without cease— people increasingly revered him for this.
translations.idiomatic: He lived with upright purity; neither wife nor children ever saw him show pleasure or vexation; day and night he taught and recited without rest, and the world honored him all the more for it.

sentences.zh: 卒於家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home.

sentences.zh: 璩所著文章二十卷，門人劉暾集而錄之。

translations.literal: Qu's collected writings ran to twenty fascicles, compiled and recorded by his disciple Liu Tun.
translations.idiomatic: His writings, twenty fascicles in all, were gathered and copied by his disciple Liu Tun.

sentences.zh: 劉慧斐

translations.literal: Liu Huifei
translations.idiomatic: Liu Huifei

sentences.zh: 劉慧斐字宣文，彭城人也。

translations.literal: Liu Huifei, courtesy name Xuanwen, was a native of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Huifei, style name Xuanwen, came from Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 父元直，淮南太守。

translations.literal: His father Yuanzhi was Administrator of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuanzhi served as Administrator of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 慧斐少博學，能屬文，起家梁安成王法曹行參軍。

translations.literal: Huifei was broadly learned from youth and skilled at composition; he first entered service as Acting Adjunct in the Law Bureau under the Prince of Ancheng of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Huifei was widely learned and adept at writing; he began his career as Acting Adjunct in the Law Bureau under the Prince of Ancheng of Liang.

sentences.zh: 嘗還都，途經尋陽，游于匡山，遇處士張孝秀，相得甚歡，遂有終焉之志。

translations.literal: Once returning to the capital, he passed through Xunyang and visited Mount Lu, where he met the recluse Zhang Xiaoxiu; they took to each other greatly and he formed the resolve to end his days there.
translations.idiomatic: Once, on his way back to the capital, he passed through Xunyang and wandered on Mount Lu, where he met the recluse Zhang Xiaoxiu; they became fast friends, and he resolved to spend the rest of his life there.

sentences.zh: 因不仕，居東林寺。

translations.literal: Therefore he did not serve and lived at Donglin Temple.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore withdrew from office and made his home at Donglin Temple.

sentences.zh: 又於山北構園一所，號曰離垢園，時人仍謂為離垢先生。

translations.literal: He also built a garden north of the mountain called the Garden of Departing Defilement, and people called him the Master of Departing Defilement.
translations.idiomatic: North of the mountain he also built a garden called the Garden of Departing Defilement, and people came to call him the Master of Departing Defilement.

sentences.zh: 慧斐尤明釋典，工篆隸，在山手寫佛經二千餘卷，常所誦者百餘卷。

translations.literal: Huifei was especially learned in Buddhist scriptures, skilled in seal and clerical scripts; in the mountains he copied more than two thousand fascicles of sutras by hand, and those he regularly recited numbered over a hundred fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: Huifei was especially versed in Buddhist scriptures and skilled in seal and clerical script; in the mountains he hand-copied more than two thousand fascicles of sutras, and more than a hundred fascicles he recited regularly.

sentences.zh: 晝夜行道，孜孜不怠，遠近欽慕之。

translations.literal: By day and night he practiced the Way tirelessly, and people near and far admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Day and night he practiced the Way without slackening, and people far and near looked up to him.

sentences.zh: 簡文臨江州，遺以几杖。

translations.literal: When Jianwen held Jiangzhou, he sent him a seat and staff as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: When Jianwen governed Jiangzhou, he sent Huifei a seat and staff as gifts.

sentences.zh: 論者雲，自遠法師沒後將二百年，始有張、劉之盛矣。

translations.literal: Commentators said that nearly two hundred years after Master Huiyuan's death, the brilliance of Zhang and Liu had at last appeared.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators said that nearly two hundred years after Master Huiyuan's death, the eminence of Zhang and Liu had at last returned.

sentences.zh: 元帝及武陵王等書問不絕。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan, the Prince of Wuling, and others sent him letters of inquiry without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan, the Prince of Wuling, and others wrote to him in an unbroken stream.

sentences.zh: 大同三年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the third year of Datong.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Datong.

sentences.zh: 慧斐兄慧鏡，安成內史。

translations.literal: Huifei's elder brother Huijing was Interior Secretary of Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Huifei's elder brother Huijing served as Interior Secretary of Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 初，元直居郡得罪，慧鏡曆詣朝士乞哀，懇惻甚至，遂以孝聞。

translations.literal: Initially Yuanzhi offended while in office; Huijing went repeatedly to court officials begging mercy with utmost earnestness, and thereby became known for filial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: At first Yuanzhi committed an offense while serving in the commandery; Huijing went again and again to court officials to plead for mercy with the deepest earnestness, and thereby won renown for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 子曇淨字元光，篤行有父風，解褐安成王國左常侍。

translations.literal: His son Tanjing, courtesy name Yuanguang, was devoted in conduct and shared his father's character; upon first appointment he became Left Regular Attendant in the Principality of Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tanjing, style name Yuanguang, was steadfast in conduct and inherited his father's ways; upon entering office he became Left Regular Attendant in the Principality of Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 父卒于郡，曇淨奔喪，不食飲者累日，絕而又蘇，每哭輒嘔血。

translations.literal: When his father died in office, Tanjing rushed home for the mourning; for many days he took no food or drink, fainting and reviving; each time he wept he vomited blood.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died while serving in the commandery, Tanjing hurried home for the funeral; for days on end he ate and drank nothing, fainting and coming to again, and each time he wept he brought up blood.

sentences.zh: 服闋，因毀成疾。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, grief had ruined his health.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning period ended, his body had been broken by grief.

sentences.zh: 會有詔士姓各舉四科，曇淨叔父慧斐舉以應孝行，武帝用為海寧令。

translations.literal: When an edict called for men of noble families to recommend candidates in four categories, his uncle Huifei nominated him for filial conduct, and Emperor Wu appointed him Magistrate of Haining.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict ordered each gentry house to recommend men in four categories, his uncle Huifei nominated him for filial conduct, and Emperor Wu appointed him magistrate of Haining.

sentences.zh: 曇淨又以兄未為縣，因以讓兄，乃除安西參軍。

translations.literal: Tanjing, because his elder brother had not yet been given a county post, yielded the appointment to his brother and was instead made Aide of Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: Because his elder brother had not yet received a county appointment, Tanjing yielded the magistracy to him and was instead made Aide of Anxi.

sentences.zh: 父亡後，事母尤淳至，身營餐粥，不以委人。

translations.literal: After his father's death he served his mother with especial sincerity, personally preparing meals and porridge, never delegating the task.
translations.idiomatic: After his father died he tended his mother with the utmost devotion, preparing her meals and porridge himself and never leaving the work to others.

sentences.zh: 母疾，衣不解帶，及母亡，水漿不入口者殆一旬。

translations.literal: When she fell ill he never undressed at her bedside; after she died he took no water or food for nearly ten days.
translations.idiomatic: When she fell ill he never loosened his clothes at her bedside; after she died he took neither food nor drink for nearly ten days.

sentences.zh: 母喪權瘞藥王寺，時天寒，曇淨身衣單布衣，廬於瘞所。

translations.literal: For her mourning he had her provisionally buried at Medicine King Temple; though the weather was cold, Tanjing wore only a single layer of cloth and lodged at the burial place in a hut.
translations.idiomatic: He had his mother provisionally buried at Medicine King Temple; though the weather was bitterly cold, Tanjing wore only a single layer of cloth and kept a mourning hut at the grave.

sentences.zh: 晝夜哭臨不絕聲，哀感行路，未期而卒。

translations.literal: Day and night he wailed without cease; passersby were moved by his grief, and before the year was out he died.
translations.idiomatic: Day and night he wept at the grave without pause; travelers were moved by his grief, and he died before the mourning year was complete.

sentences.zh: 范元琰

translations.literal: Fan Yuanyan
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yuanyan

sentences.zh: 范元琰字伯珪，一字長玉，吳郡錢塘人也。

translations.literal: Fan Yuanyan, courtesy name Bogui, alternate name Changyu, was a native of Qiantang in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yuanyan, style name Bogui, also called Changyu, came from Qiantang in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖悅之，太學博士征，不至。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yuezhi was summoned as Erudite of the Imperial Academy but did not go.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yuezhi was summoned to serve as Erudite of the Imperial Academy but declined to go.

sentences.zh: 父靈瑜，居父憂以毀卒。

translations.literal: His father Lingyu, while in mourning for his father, died from grief's devastation.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lingyu, while mourning his own father, died from the ruin of excessive grief.

sentences.zh: 元琰時童孺，哀慕盡禮，親黨異之。

translations.literal: Yuanyan was still a child yet mourned with complete propriety, astonishing kin and neighbors.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyan was still a small child, yet he mourned with full propriety, and relatives and neighbors marveled at him.

sentences.zh: 及長好學，博通經史，兼精佛義，然謙敬不以所長驕人。

translations.literal: When grown he loved learning, mastered classics and histories, and was also versed in Buddhist doctrine, yet remained humble and never flaunted his strengths before others.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up he loved learning, mastered the classics and histories, and was also well versed in Buddhist teaching, yet he remained modest and never lorded his talents over others.

sentences.zh: 祖母患癰，恒自含吮。

translations.literal: When his grandmother suffered from an abscess, he constantly sucked it himself.
translations.idiomatic: When his grandmother had an abscess, he always sucked it out himself.

sentences.zh: 與人言常恐傷物。

translations.literal: In conversation he always feared to harm others.
translations.idiomatic: In speaking with others he always feared to cause hurt.

sentences.zh: 居家不出城市，雖獨居如對賓客，見者莫不改容憚之。

translations.literal: He stayed home and did not enter the city; even alone he conducted himself as though facing guests, and all who saw him changed expression and stood in awe.
translations.idiomatic: He kept to his home and did not go into the city; even when alone he behaved as though guests were present, and all who saw him changed countenance and stood in awe.

sentences.zh: 家貧，唯以園蔬為業。

translations.literal: The family was poor; he made his living solely from garden vegetables.
translations.idiomatic: The family was poor, and he supported himself only by growing garden vegetables.

sentences.zh: 嘗出行，見人盜其菘，元琰遽退走。

translations.literal: Once going out, he saw someone stealing his greens; Yuanyan hurriedly withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Once when he went out, he saw someone stealing his cabbages; Yuanyan quickly turned away and left.

sentences.zh: 母問其故，具以實答。

translations.literal: His mother asked the reason and he told her the whole truth.
translations.idiomatic: His mother asked why, and he told her the whole truth.

sentences.zh: 母問盜者為誰，答曰：「向所以退，畏其愧恥，今啟其名，願不泄也。

translations.literal: When his mother asked who the thief was, he answered: "I withdrew earlier because I feared shaming him; now that you ask his name, I beg you not to reveal it.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother asked who the thief was, he answered, "I withdrew because I feared shaming him; now that you ask his name, I beg you not to disclose it.

sentences.zh: 」於是母子秘之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon mother and son kept the matter secret.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon mother and son kept the secret between them.

sentences.zh: 或有涉溝盜其筍者，元琰因伐木為橋以度之，自是盜者大慚，一鄉無復草竊。

translations.literal: When someone crossed a ditch to steal his bamboo shoots, Yuanyan cut timber to build a bridge so they could cross; thereafter the thieves felt great shame, and the whole village ceased petty theft.
translations.idiomatic: When someone crossed a ditch to steal his bamboo shoots, Yuanyan cut wood and built a bridge so they could cross; after that the thieves were deeply ashamed, and the whole village gave up petty theft.

sentences.zh: 齊建武初，徵為曹武平西參軍，不至。

translations.literal: Early in Jianwu of Qi he was summoned as Aide on the Pacify-West campaign under Cao Wu but did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianwu era of Qi he was summoned to serve as Aide on Cao Wu's Pacify-West campaign but declined to go.

sentences.zh: 于時始安王遙光為揚州，謂徐孝嗣曰：「曹武參軍，豈是禮賢之職。

translations.literal: At that time Prince Shi'an of Shi'an was inspector of Yangzhou; he said to Xu Xiaosi: "An aide under Cao Wu— is that a post for honoring the worthy?
translations.idiomatic: At that time Prince Shi'an of Shi'an was inspector of Yangzhou; he said to Xu Xiaosi, "An aide under Cao Wu— is that a post fit for honoring a man of worth?

sentences.zh: 」欲以西曹書佐聘之，會遙光敗，不果，時人以為恨。

translations.literal: " He wished to engage him as Western Bureau Secretary, but Shi'an's faction fell before it happened; contemporaries regarded it as a regret.
translations.idiomatic: " He meant to engage Yuanyan as Western Bureau Secretary, but Shi'an's faction fell before it could happen; people of the time counted it a loss.

sentences.zh: 沛國劉瓛深加器異，嘗表稱之。

translations.literal: Liu Huan of Pei deeply admired him and once submitted a memorial praising him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Huan of Pei held him in high esteem and once submitted a memorial commending him.

sentences.zh: 天監九年，縣令管慧辯上言義行，揚州刺史臨川王宏辟命，不至。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Tianjian the magistrate Guan Huibian reported his righteous conduct; the Inspector of Yangzhou, Prince Linchuan Hong, offered him appointment but he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Tianjian the magistrate Guan Huibian reported his moral conduct; Prince Linchuan Hong, inspector of Yangzhou, offered him an appointment, but he did not accept.

sentences.zh: 卒於家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home.

sentences.zh: 庾詵字彥寶，新野人也。

translations.literal: Yu Shen, courtesy name Yanbao, was a native of Xinye.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shen, style name Yanbao, came from Xinye.

sentences.zh: 幼聰警篤學，經史百家，無不該綜。

translations.literal: Clever and alert from childhood, devoted to study; the classics, histories, and the hundred schools— none he did not comprehend.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he was clever and alert and devoted to learning; among the classics, histories, and the hundred schools there was nothing he had not mastered.

sentences.zh: 緯候書射，棋算機巧，並一時之絕。

translations.literal: Astronomy, apocrypha, calligraphy, archery, chess, calculation, and mechanical ingenuity— all were unrivaled in his day.
translations.idiomatic: In astronomy, apocryphal texts, calligraphy, archery, chess, calculation, and mechanical ingenuity he was unmatched in his time.

sentences.zh: 而性托夷簡，特愛林泉，十畝之宅，山池居半。

translations.literal: Yet his nature leaned toward ease and simplicity; he especially loved forests and springs; of his ten-acre homestead, hills and ponds occupied half.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his temperament was easy and plain; he especially loved woods and streams, and of his ten-acre home, hills and ponds took up half.

sentences.zh: 蔬食弊衣，不修產業。

translations.literal: Vegetarian food and worn clothes; he did not tend to property or business.
translations.idiomatic: He ate plain vegetables and wore threadbare clothes and did not pursue wealth or property.

sentences.zh: 遇火，止出書數簣坐于池上，有為火來者，答云：「唯恐損竹」。

translations.literal: When fire broke out, he took out only a few bundles of books and sat on the pond; when someone came because of the fire, he answered: "I only fear harm to the bamboo."
translations.idiomatic: When a fire broke out, he carried out only a few bundles of books and sat on the pond; when someone came because of the fire, he replied, "I only fear damage to the bamboo."

sentences.zh: 乘舟從沮中山舍還，載米一百五十石。

translations.literal: Returning by boat from a lodge at Mount Ju, he loaded a hundred and fifty shi of rice.
translations.idiomatic: Returning by boat from a lodge on Mount Ju, he loaded a hundred and fifty shi of rice.

sentences.zh: 有人寄載三十石，及至宅，寄載者曰：「君三十斛，我百五十斛。

translations.literal: Someone asked to ship thirty shi along; when they reached home the fellow said: "Your thirty hu, my hundred fifty hu.
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked to ship thirty shi along with him; when they reached home the fellow said, "Your thirty hu, my hundred fifty hu.

sentences.zh: 」詵默然不言，恣其取足。

translations.literal: " Shen said nothing and let him take as much as he wanted.
translations.idiomatic: " Shen remained silent and let him take as much as he pleased.

sentences.zh: 鄰人有被誣為盜，見劾妄款。

translations.literal: A neighbor was falsely accused as a thief; he was impeached and made a false confession.
translations.idiomatic: A neighbor had been falsely accused of theft and, when impeached, confessed under duress to crimes he had not committed.

sentences.zh: 詵矜之，乃以書質錢二萬，令門生詐為其親，代之酬備。

translations.literal: Shen took pity on him; he then pawned books for twenty thousand cash and had a student pose as the man's relative to pay compensation in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: Shen took pity on him, pawned his books for twenty thousand cash, and had a student pose as the man's kinsman to pay the compensation on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 鄰人獲免謝詵，詵曰：「吾矜天下無辜，豈期謝也。」

translations.literal: The neighbor was spared and thanked Shen. Shen said: "I pity the innocent throughout the world—how could I expect thanks?"
translations.idiomatic: When the neighbor was cleared and came to thank him, Shen said, "I pity every innocent person under heaven. How could I have expected thanks?"

sentences.zh: 梁武帝少與詵善，及起兵，署為平西府記室參軍，詵不屈。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang was friendly with Shen in youth; when he raised troops he appointed him Recorder of the Pacify-the-West Headquarters, but Shen would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Emperor Wu of Liang had been on good terms with Shen; when he raised an army he appointed Shen recorder of the Pacify-the-West headquarters, but Shen refused the post.

sentences.zh: 平生少所遊狎，河東柳惲欲與交，拒而弗納。

translations.literal: In life he had few intimate companions; Liu Yun of Hedong wished to befriend him, but was refused and not admitted.
translations.idiomatic: He had few intimate associates in his life; Liu Yun of Hedong sought his friendship, but Shen declined and would not accept him.

sentences.zh: 普通中，詔以為黃門侍郎，稱疾不起。

translations.literal: During the Putong era an edict appointing him Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates came, but he claimed illness and did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: During the Putong era he was ordered to serve as Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates, but he pleaded illness and did not take up the post.

sentences.zh: 晚年尤遵釋教，宅內立道場，環繞禮懺，六時不輟。

translations.literal: In his later years he especially followed the Buddhist teaching; within his residence he established a chapel, circumambulating and performing repentance six times daily without cease.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he devoted himself especially to Buddhism; he established a chapel in his home and circled it in worship and repentance six times a day without interruption.

sentences.zh: 誦法華經，每日一遍。

translations.literal: He recited the Lotus Sutra once every day.
translations.idiomatic: Each day he recited the Lotus Sutra once through.

sentences.zh: 後夜中忽見一道人自稱願公，容止甚異，呼詵為上行先生，授香而去。

translations.literal: Later, in the middle of the night, he suddenly saw a Daoist priest who called himself Master Yuan; his bearing was very unusual. He addressed Shen as Master Shangxing, gave him incense, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Later one night he suddenly saw a Daoist priest who called himself Master Yuan; the man's bearing was strikingly unusual. He addressed Shen as Master Shangxing, gave him incense, and left.

sentences.zh: 中大通四年，因寢忽驚覺，曰：「願公復來，不可久住。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhongdatong, while sleeping he suddenly awoke with a start and said: "Master Yuan has come again; I cannot stay long.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhongdatong he woke with a start from sleep and said, "Master Yuan has come again; I cannot remain long.

sentences.zh: 」顏色不變，言終而亡，年七十八。

translations.literal: " His complexion did not change; when he finished speaking he died, aged seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: " His face did not change; when he had finished speaking he died, at the age of seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 舉室咸聞空中唱「上行先生已生彌陀淨域矣」。

translations.literal: The whole household all heard a voice in the air proclaim: "Master Shangxing has been born into Amitabha's Pure Land."
translations.idiomatic: Everyone in the household heard a voice in the air declare, "Master Shangxing has been born into Amitabha's Pure Land."

sentences.zh: 武帝聞而下詔，諡貞節處士，以顯高烈。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu heard of it he issued an edict, conferring the posthumous title Reclusive Gentleman of Pure Integrity to display his lofty virtue.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu heard of it he issued an edict, giving Shen the posthumous title Reclusive Gentleman of Pure Integrity to honor his exalted character.

sentences.zh: 詵所撰帝曆二十卷，易林二十卷，續伍端休江陵記一卷，晉朝雜事五卷，總抄八十卷，行於世。

translations.literal: Works composed by Shen included Imperial Calendar in twenty scrolls, Forest of Changes in twenty scrolls, Continuation of Wu Duanxiu's Record of Jiangling in one scroll, Miscellaneous Matters of the Jin Dynasty in five scrolls, and General Extracts in eighty scrolls—all circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Shen authored the Imperial Calendar in twenty scrolls, the Forest of Changes in twenty scrolls, a continuation of Wu Duanxiu's Record of Jiangling in one scroll, Miscellaneous Matters of the Jin Dynasty in five scrolls, and General Extracts in eighty scrolls, all of which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 子曼倩字世華，亦早有令譽。

translations.literal: His son Manqian, courtesy name Shihua, also early gained a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: His son Manqian, styled Shihua, also won an excellent reputation at an early age.

sentences.zh: 元帝在荊州，為中錄事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan was in Jingzhou, he served as Central Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Yuan was in Jingzhou, Manqian served as Central Recorder.

sentences.zh: 每出，帝常目送之，謂劉之遴曰：「荊南信多君子。

translations.literal: Whenever he went out, the Emperor would follow him with his gaze; he said to Liu Zhilin: "South of Jing truly has many gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Manqian went out, the emperor would watch him depart and say to Liu Zhilin, "South of Jing truly has many men of worth.

sentences.zh: 」後轉諮議參軍。

translations.literal: " Later he was transferred to Advisory Aide.
translations.idiomatic: " Later he was transferred to the post of Advisory Aide.

sentences.zh: 所著喪服儀，文字體例，老子義疏，算經及七曜曆術，並所制文章，凡九十五卷。

translations.literal: Works he authored—the Mourning Rites Ceremonies, Textual Norms, Exegesis of Laozi, Calculation Classic and the Seven Luminaries Calendar Arts, together with essays he composed—totaled ninety-five scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: His writings—the Mourning Rites Ceremonies, Textual Norms, an exegesis of Laozi, the Calculation Classic and the arts of the Seven Luminaries calendrics, together with his own compositions—amounted to ninety-five scrolls in all.

sentences.zh: 子季才有學行，承聖中，位中書侍郎。

translations.literal: His son Jicai had learning and virtue; during the Chengsheng era he held the post of Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jicai was a man of learning and integrity; during the Chengsheng era he served as Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 江陵平，隨例入長安。

translations.literal: When Jiangling was pacified, he entered Chang'an according to the usual practice.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangling fell he was taken to Chang'an along with the others.

sentences.zh: 張孝秀

translations.literal: Zhang Xiaoxiu
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xiaoxiu

sentences.zh: 張孝秀字文逸，南陽宛人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Xiaoxiu, courtesy name Wenyi, was a native of Wan in Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xiaoxiu, styled Wenyi, was from Wan in Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 徙居尋陽。

translations.literal: He moved to live at Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: His family moved to Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 曾祖須無，祖僧監，父希，並別駕從事。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Xu Wu, grandfather Sengjian, and father Xi all served as staff officers under Vice Governors.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Xu Wu, his grandfather Sengjian, and his father Xi had all served as staff officers under regional vice governors.

sentences.zh: 孝秀長六尺餘，白皙美鬚眉，仕州中從事史。

translations.literal: Xiaoxiu was over six chi in height, fair-skinned with fine beard and brows; he served as a Staff Officer of the province.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoxiu stood more than six chi tall, with fair skin and handsome beard and brows; he served as a staff officer in the provincial administration.

sentences.zh: 遇刺史陳伯之叛，孝秀與州中士大夫謀襲之，事覺，逃于盆水側。

translations.literal: When the Regional Inspector Chen Bozhi rebelled, Xiaoxiu and the gentry of the province plotted to attack him; the affair was discovered and he fled to the banks of the Pen River.
translations.idiomatic: When the regional inspector Chen Bozhi rebelled, Xiaoxiu and the province's literati plotted to seize him; when the plot was discovered he fled to the banks of the Pen River.

sentences.zh: 有商人置諸褚中，輾轉入東林。

translations.literal: A merchant hid him in a trunk and, passing from hand to hand, brought him to Donglin.
translations.idiomatic: A merchant hid him in a trunk and, conveyed from place to place, he eventually reached Donglin.

sentences.zh: 伯之得其母郭，以蠟灌殺之。

translations.literal: Bozhi seized his mother, Lady Guo, and killed her by pouring wax down her throat.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhi captured his mother, Lady Guo, and killed her by pouring molten wax down her throat.

sentences.zh: 孝秀遣妻妾，入匡山修行學道。

translations.literal: Xiaoxiu sent away wife and concubines and entered Mount Kuang to cultivate the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoxiu dismissed his wife and concubines and went to Mount Kuang to practice the Way.

sentences.zh: 服闋，建安王召為別駕。

translations.literal: When mourning was complete, Prince Jian'an summoned him as Vice Governor's aide.
translations.idiomatic: After his mourning period ended, Prince Jian'an summoned him to serve as vice governor's aide.

sentences.zh: 因去職歸山，居於東林寺，有田數十頃，部曲數百人，率以力田，盡供山眾。

translations.literal: He then left office and returned to the mountains, dwelling at Donglin Temple; he possessed several dozen qing of farmland and several hundred retainers, all of whom he put to tilling, entirely supplying the monastic community.
translations.idiomatic: He then resigned and returned to the mountains, living at Donglin Temple; he owned several dozen qing of farmland and several hundred household retainers, whom he set to farming and whose entire yield he gave to the monastic community.

sentences.zh: 遠近歸慕，赴之如市。

translations.literal: From near and far people admired him and came to him as to a market.
translations.idiomatic: People from near and far admired him and flocked to him in crowds.

sentences.zh: 孝秀性通率，不好浮華，常冠谷皮巾，躡蒲履，手執並閭皮麈尾，服寒食散，盛冬臥于石上。

translations.literal: Xiaoxiu's nature was open and plain; he disliked ostentation. He habitually wore a grain-husk cap, trod reed sandals, held a fly-whisk of birch-leather in hand, took cold-food powder, and even in deep winter slept on stone.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoxiu was frank and unpretentious and disliked show; he usually wore a grain-husk cap and reed sandals, carried a birch-leather fly-whisk, took cold-food powder, and even in the depth of winter slept on bare stone.

sentences.zh: 博涉群書，專精釋典。

translations.literal: He read widely among all books and specialized in Buddhist scriptures.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely and devoted himself especially to Buddhist scripture.

sentences.zh: 僧有虧戒律者，集眾佛前，作羯磨而笞之，多能改過。

translations.literal: When monks broke precepts, he assembled the community before the Buddha and, performing karmavācā, flogged them; many were able to reform.
translations.idiomatic: When monks violated the precepts he assembled the community before the Buddha, held a formal ecclesiastical proceeding, and had them flogged; many thereby reformed.

sentences.zh: 善談論，工隸書，凡諸藝能，莫不明習。

translations.literal: He was skilled in discourse, adept at clerical script, and in every art and ability there was none he did not know well.
translations.idiomatic: He was an accomplished speaker, skilled at clerical script, and proficient in every art he touched.

sentences.zh: 普通三年卒，室中皆聞非常香。

translations.literal: He died in the third year of Putong; an extraordinary fragrance pervaded the room.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Putong, and everyone in the room smelled an extraordinary fragrance.

sentences.zh: 梁簡文甚傷悼焉，與劉慧斐書，述其貞白雲。

translations.literal: Emperor Jianwen of Liang was deeply grieved and wrote to Liu Huifei describing his pure integrity with admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jianwen of Liang grieved deeply over his death and wrote to Liu Huifei praising his pure and upright character.

sentences.zh: 庾承先

translations.literal: Yu Chengxian
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chengxian

sentences.zh: 庾承先字子通，潁川鄢陵人也。

translations.literal: Yu Chengxian, courtesy name Zitong, was a native of Yanling in Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chengxian, styled Zitong, was from Yanling in Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 少沈靜有志操，是非不涉於言，喜慍不形於色，人莫能窺也。

translations.literal: From youth he was quiet and steady with firm principles; right and wrong did not enter his speech, joy and anger did not show on his face—no one could fathom him.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was quiet and resolute; he did not speak of others' faults, joy and anger never showed on his face, and no one could read his thoughts.

sentences.zh: 弱歲受學于南陽劉虯，強記敏識，出於群輩。

translations.literal: In early youth he studied under Liu Hu of Nanyang; with powerful memory and keen perception he stood above his peers.
translations.idiomatic: In his early youth he studied under Liu Hu of Nanyang; his powerful memory and quick wit set him above his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 玄經釋典，靡不該悉；

translations.literal: Dark Classics and Buddhist scriptures—none he did not comprehend thoroughly;
translations.idiomatic: Dark learning and Buddhist scripture—there was none he had not mastered thoroughly;

sentences.zh: 九流七略，咸所精練。

translations.literal: the Nine Currents and Seven Summaries—all he refined and mastered.
translations.idiomatic: the Nine Currents and the Seven Summaries—he had trained in them all.

sentences.zh: 辟功曹不就，乃與道士王僧鎮同游衡嶽。

translations.literal: Summoned as Merit Officer he did not accept; then he traveled Mount Heng together with the Daoist Wang Shenzhen.
translations.idiomatic: When summoned as merit officer he declined; he then traveled Mount Heng with the Daoist Wang Shenzhen.

sentences.zh: 晚以弟疾還鄉里，遂居土臺山。

translations.literal: In later years, because his younger brother was ill, he returned home and then dwelt on Mount Tutai.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when his younger brother fell ill, he returned to his native place and settled on Mount Tutai.

sentences.zh: 梁鄱陽忠烈王在州，欽其風味，要與遊處，令講老子。

translations.literal: When Prince Zhonglie of Poyang of Liang was in the province he admired his character, invited him to associate and travel together, and had him lecture on Laozi.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Zhonglie of Poyang was regional inspector he admired Chengxian's character, invited him to keep company, and had him lecture on the Laozi.

sentences.zh: 遠近名僧，咸來赴集，論難鋒起，異端競至，承先徐相酬答，皆得所未聞。

translations.literal: Eminent monks from near and far all came to gather; debate flared like blades, heterodox views competed to arrive; Chengxian slowly responded in turn and all obtained what they had never heard.
translations.idiomatic: Eminent monks from near and far all came; sharp debate arose and unorthodox views poured forth, yet Chengxian answered each point at leisure, and everyone heard things they had never encountered before.

sentences.zh: 忠烈王尤所欽重。

translations.literal: Prince Zhonglie especially esteemed and valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhonglie held him in especially high regard.

sentences.zh: 中大通三年，廬山劉慧斐至荊州，承先與之有舊，往從之，荊陝學徒因請承先講老子。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhongdatong, Liu Huifei of Mount Lu arrived in Jingzhou; Chengxian had old ties with him and went to follow him; students of Jing and Shan therefore asked Chengxian to lecture on Laozi.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhongdatong, Liu Huifei of Mount Lu came to Jingzhou; Chengxian had known him of old and went to join him, and students in Jing and Shan asked Chengxian to lecture on the Laozi.

sentences.zh: 湘東王親命駕臨聽，論議終日，留連月餘，乃還山。

translations.literal: Prince Xiangdong personally ordered his carriage and came to listen; discussion lasted the whole day; he lingered more than a month before returning to the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiangdong came in person to listen; debates ran all day, and he stayed for more than a month before Chengxian returned to the mountain.

sentences.zh: 王親祖道，並贈篇什，隱者美之。

translations.literal: The Prince personally saw him off on the road and also presented poems; recluses praised this.
translations.idiomatic: The prince saw him off in person and also gave him poems, which recluses admired.

sentences.zh: 其年卒，刺史厚有贈賻。

translations.literal: That year he died; the regional inspector gave a generous funeral gift.
translations.idiomatic: He died that same year, and the regional inspector gave a generous funeral gift.

sentences.zh: 門人黃士龍讓曰：「先師平素食不求飽，衣不求輕，凡有贈遺，皆無所受。

translations.literal: His disciple Huang Shilong declined, saying: "Our late master in life did not seek to eat his fill or dress lightly; whenever gifts were offered he never accepted any.
translations.idiomatic: His disciple Huang Shilong declined, saying, "Our late master in life did not seek to eat his fill or dress in finery; he never accepted anything that was given him.

sentences.zh: 臨終之日，誡約家門，薄棺周形，巾褐為斂。

translations.literal: On the day of his death he admonished his household: a plain coffin with rounded form, burial in cap and brown robe.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he charged his household to give him a plain coffin with rounded corners and to bury him in cap and brown robes.

sentences.zh: 雖蒙賚及，不敢輕承教旨，以違平生之操。

translations.literal: Though we have received these imperial gifts, we dare not lightly accept contrary to his teaching and violate his lifelong principles.
translations.idiomatic: Though we have received these gifts, we dare not lightly accept them in violation of his instructions and his lifelong principles.

sentences.zh: 錢布輒付使反。

translations.literal: The cash and cloth we at once hand back to the messenger to return.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore return the money and cloth to the messenger at once.

sentences.zh: 」時論高之。

translations.literal: " The opinion of the day held this in high esteem.
translations.idiomatic: " Contemporaries praised this highly.

sentences.zh: 馬樞字要理，扶風郿人也。

translations.literal: Ma Shu, courtesy name Yaoli, was a native of Mei in Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shu, styled Yaoli, was from Mei in Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 祖靈慶，齊竟陵王錄事參軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Lingqing served as Recording Secretary on the staff of Prince Jingling of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Lingqing had served as recording secretary on the staff of Prince Jingling of Qi.

sentences.zh: 樞數歲而孤，為其姑所養。

translations.literal: Shu was orphaned at several years of age and was raised by his paternal aunt.
translations.idiomatic: Shu lost his father when he was still a child and was raised by his paternal aunt.

sentences.zh: 六歲，能誦孝經、論語、老子。

translations.literal: At six years he could recite the Classic of Filial Piety, the Analects, and Laozi.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of six he could recite the Classic of Filial Piety, the Analects, and the Laozi.

sentences.zh: 及長，博極經史，尤善佛經及周易、老子義。

translations.literal: When grown, he exhaustively mastered the classics and histories; he especially excelled in Buddhist scriptures and the meanings of the Changes and Laozi.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up he mastered the classics and histories, and was especially adept at Buddhist scriptures and the exegesis of the Changes and Laozi.

sentences.zh: 梁邵陵王綸為南徐州刺史，素聞其名，引為學士。

translations.literal: When Prince Shaoling Lun of Liang was Regional Inspector of South Xuzhou, having long heard his name, he brought him in as a Scholar.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Shaoling Lun of Liang was governor of South Xuzhou, having long heard of his reputation, he invited him to serve as a scholar on his staff.

sentences.zh: 綸時自講大品經，令樞講維摩、老子、周易，同日發題，道俗聽者二千人。

translations.literal: Lun then lectured on the Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra himself and had Shu lecture on the Vimalakīrti, Laozi, and Changes, all opening topics on the same day; lay and clerical listeners numbered two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Lun himself lectured on the Great Perfection of Wisdom Sutra while assigning Shu to lecture on the Vimalakīrti Sutra, the Laozi, and the Changes on the same day; two thousand monks and laymen came to listen.

sentences.zh: 王欲極觀優劣，乃謂眾曰：「與馬學士論義，必使屈服，不得空立客主。

translations.literal: The Prince wished to observe superiority and inferiority to the full; he then said to the assembly: "In debating doctrine with Scholar Ma, you must make him submit—do not simply stand as guest and host in empty formality.
translations.idiomatic: The prince wished to test every side to the limit and said to the assembly, "In debating doctrine with Scholar Ma you must try to defeat him; do not merely play at guest and host in empty ceremony.

sentences.zh: 」於是數家學者，各起問端。

translations.literal: " Thereupon several schools of scholars each raised probing questions.
translations.idiomatic: " Several groups of scholars then each opened with challenging questions.

sentences.zh: 樞乃依次剖判，開其宗旨，然後枝分派別，轉變無窮，論者拱默聽受而已，綸甚嘉之。

translations.literal: Shu then analyzed them in order, opened their essential doctrines, and then branched and divided them in endless variation; the debaters could only bow in silence and listen—Lun greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Shu answered them one by one, stated each school's central doctrine, then branched into finer distinctions in endlessly shifting turns; the debaters could only bow in silence and listen, and Lun was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 尋遇侯景之亂，綸舉兵援台，乃留書二萬卷付樞。

translations.literal: Soon he encountered the rebellion of Hou Jing; Lun raised troops to relieve the capital and left twenty thousand scrolls of books with Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the rebellion of Hou Jing broke out; Lun raised an army to relieve the capital and entrusted twenty thousand scrolls of books to Shu.

sentences.zh: 樞肆志尋覽，殆將周遍，乃喟然歎曰：「吾聞貴爵位者以巢、由為桎梏，愛山林者以伊、呂為管庫，束名實則芻芥柱下之言，翫清虛則糠秕席上之說，稽之篤論，亦各從其好也。

translations.literal: Shu gave free rein to searching and reading until he had nearly covered all; he then sighed deeply and said: "I have heard that those who prize rank and office regard Chao and Xu as shackles, while those who love mountains and forests regard Yi and Lü as storehouse keepers; binding fame and substance makes Zhuangzi's words chaff, playing with emptiness and purity makes Confucian teaching bran—examining solid doctrine, each follows his own preference.
translations.idiomatic: Shu read through them at will until he had nearly covered the whole collection, then sighed and said, "I have heard that those who prize rank and office treat Chao and Xu as shackles, while those who love mountains and forests treat Yi and Lü as mere storekeepers; those who bind themselves to fame treat Laozi's words as chaff, while those who play at purity treat Confucian doctrine as bran—yet when one weighs serious doctrine, each follows his own inclination.

sentences.zh: 比求志之士，望塗而息，豈天之不惠高尚，何山林之無聞甚乎。

translations.literal: Nowadays seekers of purpose halt at the roadside—is Heaven not kind to the lofty-minded? Why is it that the mountains and forests are so little heard of?
translations.idiomatic: Yet now those who seek a higher purpose turn back at the threshold—has Heaven no favor for the lofty-minded? Why are the mountains and forests so utterly forgotten?

sentences.zh: 」乃隱于茅山，有終焉之志。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he went into seclusion on Mount Mao, with the intention of ending his days there.
translations.idiomatic: " He then withdrew to Mount Mao, resolved to end his days there.

sentences.zh: 樞少屬亂離，凡所居處，盜賊不入，依託者常數百家。

translations.literal: Shu from youth belonged to times of chaos and separation; wherever he dwelt, bandits did not enter; dependents often numbered several hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Shu lived through disorder; wherever he settled bandits did not intrude, and several hundred households regularly sought refuge with him.

sentences.zh: 目精洞黃，能視闇中物。

translations.literal: His pupils were clear yellow and could see objects in darkness.
translations.idiomatic: His pupils were bright yellow and he could see in the dark.

sentences.zh: 有白晏一雙，巢其庭樹，馴狎橺廡，時至几案，春來秋去，幾三十年。

translations.literal: A pair of white swallows nested in his courtyard tree, tame and familiar on the eaves and verandas, sometimes coming to desk and couch; they came in spring and left in autumn for nearly thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: A pair of white swallows nested in the tree in his courtyard, grew tame enough to perch on the eaves and verandas and even come to his desk; they returned every spring and departed every autumn for nearly thirty years.

sentences.zh: 太建十三年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the thirteenth year of Taijian.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirteenth year of Taijian.

sentences.zh: 撰道覺論行於世。

translations.literal: He composed the Treatise on Awakening to the Way, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Treatise on Awakening to the Way, which circulated widely.

translations.literal: 【Discussion】
translations.idiomatic: Discussion

sentences.zh: 論曰：夫獨往之人，皆稟偏介之性，不能摧志屈道，借譽期通。

translations.literal: The treatise says: Those who go alone are all endowed with an obstinate and exceptional nature; they cannot break their resolve or bend the Way to borrow reputation and expect advancement.
translations.idiomatic: The essay observes: Men who walk alone are all endowed with an uncompromising nature; they cannot bend their will or twist the Way to borrow repute in hope of advancement.

sentences.zh: 若使夫遇見信之主，逢時來之運，豈其放情江海，取逸丘樊？

translations.literal: If such men met a lord who truly trusted them and encountered a timely destiny come, how would they release their feelings to rivers and seas or seek ease in hill and grove?
translations.idiomatic: Had they met a ruler who truly trusted them and arrived in a propitious age, would they still have given themselves to rivers and seas or sought their ease on hills and in groves?

sentences.zh: 不得已而然故也。

translations.literal: It is because they had no choice but to be so.
translations.idiomatic: They did so only because they had no choice.

sentences.zh: 且岩壑閑遠，水石清華，雖復崇門八襲，高城萬雉，莫不蓄壤開泉，髣佛林澤。

translations.literal: Moreover, cliff and ravine are tranquil and remote, water and stone pure and splendid; even though gate towers rise eightfold and high walls stand ten thousand zhi, none fail to store soil and open springs, faintly resembling forest and marsh.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, cliffs and ravines are quiet and remote, water and stone clear and splendid; even where gate towers rise in tiers and high walls stretch for miles, every estate opens springs and hoards soil until it seems almost a woodland park.

sentences.zh: 故知松山桂渚，非止素玩，碧澗清潭，翻成麗矚。

translations.literal: Thus one knows that pine-covered hills and cassia islets are not merely plain diversions; green brooks and clear pools in turn become splendid sights.
translations.idiomatic: One sees that pine hills and cassia islets were not simple pastimes alone—jade brooks and clear pools became splendid objects of admiration.

sentences.zh: 掛冕東都，夫何難之有。

translations.literal: To hang up one's crown-cap in the Eastern Capital—what difficulty is there in that?
translations.idiomatic: To hang up one's official cap in the Eastern Capital—what difficulty would there be?
